a139.speaker: Official of the Ousmane Doussou Camara school complex (unnamed)
a139.name: Official of the Ousmane Doussou Camara school complex (unnamed)
a139.speech: Explains: “it was the security forces who came and attacked a petrol station located near the school. Then they turned against the pupils. The situation is really tense.”

a139.speaker: Parents of pupils
a139.name: Parents of pupils
a139.speech: Many parents say they have still not found their children at the time the dispatch was put online.

a252.speaker: USAid foreign assistance portal (data published on the USAid website)
a252.name: USAid foreign assistance portal (data published on the USAid website)
a252.speech: Shows that Malawi was set to get $284.7 million during Fiscal Year (FY) 2024; for FY2025, the total foreign assistance budget request for the Department of State and USAid is $42.8 billion.

a252.speaker: Office of the spokesperson for US Secretary of State Marco Rubio (statement published January 26 2025)
a252.name: Office of the spokesperson for US Secretary of State Marco Rubio (statement published January 26 2025)
a252.speech: Said they have paused all foreign assistance funded by or through the State Department and USAid for review ; said Rubio was initiating a review of all foreign assistance programmes to ensure they are efficient and consistent with US foreign policy under the America First agenda.

a252.speaker: Simplex Chithyola-Banda, Malawi Minister of Finance and Economic Affairs
a252.name: Simplex Chithyola-Banda
a252.title: Malawi Minister of Finance and Economic Affairs
a252.speech: Projected grants at K1.17 trillion in the 2024/25 National Budget, of which K1.10 trillion was expected from international organisations and K72.69 billion from foreign governments.

a252.speaker: Williams Banda, spokesperson for the Ministry of Finance and Economic Affairs
a252.name: Williams Banda
a252.title: spokesperson for the Ministry of Finance and Economic Affairs
a252.speech: Said only K9.2 billion of USAid funding appears in the 2024/25 National Budget and that the US government off-budget projection in FY2024/25 was about K307 billion: “For USAid, it is only the government to government projects that are reflected in the budget framework. So, out of the K1.17 trillion, only K9.2bn is from USAid. The rest of their support is off-budget. That excludes funds for Millennium Challenge Corporation which we do not have records on projections.”

a333.speaker: Governor Mai Mala Buni of Yobe State
a333.name: Governor Mai Mala Buni of Yobe State
a333.speech: Stated that the Aliko Dangote Foundation’s (ADF) Annual Food Intervention Programme has bolstered Nigeria’s food security ; said the ADF’s food programme has played a significant role in alleviating hunger, and complemented government’s efforts toward achieving food security in the country ; said the gesture would support the government’s ongoing humanitarian efforts. “It is with great pleasure that we are here today for yet another humanitarian assistance. This is the flag-off of the distribution of 30,000 bags of 10Kg parboiled rice to further support our people, specifically the less privileged and vulnerable persons.”

a333.speaker: Governor Mai Mala Buni of Yobe State
a333.name: Governor Mai Mala Buni of Yobe State
a333.speech: Expressed appreciation to the Foundation for its sustained support to the state, especially in the areas of humanitarian aid, primary healthcare and routine immunisation programmes ; urged community and local government committees to ensure transparency and fairness in the distribution process ; said there is the need to give priority to deserving beneficiaries and warned that the government would carefully monitor the exercise.

a333.speaker: Dr. Mohammed Goje, Executive Secretary of Yobe State Emergency Management Agency (YOSEMA)
a333.name: Dr. Mohammed Goje
a333.title: Executive Secretary of Yobe State Emergency Management Agency (YOSEMA)
a333.speech: Said the agency is committed to accountability and transparency in the distribution exercise.

a333.speaker: Abubakar Muhammed, representative of the Aliko Dangote Foundation
a333.name: Abubakar Muhammed
a333.title: representative of the Aliko Dangote Foundation
a333.speech: Said the donation was part of the Foundation’s nationwide initiative to ease the economic burden on vulnerable Nigerians. “Alhaji Aliko Dangote, through his Foundation, decided to support the Yobe State government with 30,000 bags of rice to be distributed to vulnerable groups. This support also extends across the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory.”

a341.speaker: Kenny Mascarenhas Monteiro, national coordinator for Youth and Volunteering, Red Cross of Cape Verde (CVCV)
a341.name: Kenny Mascarenhas Monteiro
a341.title: national coordinator for Youth and Volunteering, Red Cross of Cape Verde (CVCV)
a341.speech: According to her, the election reinforces the organisation's commitment to involving young people in strategic and humanitarian decisions.

a492.speaker: Inspector Akinwale Oriyomi, prosecutor
a492.name: Inspector Akinwale Oriyomi
a492.title: prosecutor
a492.speech: Told the court that the incident occurred on March 15 when the defendants conspired to commit the act ; said the offence was punishable under Section 421, 69(a), 181(1)(d), of the Criminal Law of Ekiti State 2021.

a492.speaker: Barrister Olumide Olowolafe, counsel to the defendants
a492.name: Barrister Olumide Olowolafe
a492.title: counsel to the defendants
a492.speech: Urged the court to grant his client bail.

a492.speaker: Chief Magistrate Abayomi Adeosun
a492.name: Chief Magistrate Abayomi Adeosun
a492.speech: Granted the bail request in the sum of N100,000 with one surety each and adjourned the case till May 9, for hearing.

a793.speaker: Mozambique and China (joint expression at an audience in Maputo)
a793.name: Mozambique and China (joint expression at an audience in Maputo)
a793.speech: Expressed their interest in strengthening bilateral cooperation between the two countries, particularly in the industry and trade sectors, and congratulated themselves on the excellent Sino-Mozambican relations, with a visible impact on the continued strengthening of political, economic and social exchange.

a793.speaker: Maria Lucas, Mozambican Minister of Foreign Affairs and Cooperation
a793.name: Maria Lucas
a793.title: Mozambican Minister of Foreign Affairs and Cooperation
a793.speech: Praised the growth of political-diplomatic cooperation embodied in the exchange of visits at different levels, especially presidential ones ; "We are going to continue working, as we were already saying, but just to say that this year we are celebrating 50 years of Mozambique's independence" ; "We will have a celebration here in Maputo, but in China there will also be a big celebration" ; mentioned that President Chapo is already preparing the visit for 2026, adding "So, there is much celebration, and that is why your coming here, your arrival here, is very welcome by the government, by the party, but also by the Mozambican people."

a793.speaker: Maria Lucas, Mozambican Minister of Foreign Affairs and Cooperation
a793.name: Maria Lucas
a793.title: Mozambican Minister of Foreign Affairs and Cooperation
a793.speech: Acknowledged the continued support China has given Mozambique in various sectors, with emphasis on humanitarian assistance, food security and infrastructure, and thanked China for the support provided for the realisation of the President's First 100 Days Plan ; "His Excellency the President, Daniel Chapo, asked me to convey the welcome to Mozambique to our special envoy and also to inform him that he is visiting Gaza province, and also to inform him that his 100-day plan was successful because of the support that China gave" ; "Besides the support that China gave, in relation to financial support for various areas with humanitarian aid, we also laid the foundation stone for the construction of the Surgical Centre of Mozambique, which will be the largest in Mozambique."

a793.speaker: Daniel Chapo, President of Mozambique (message conveyed by Maria Lucas)
a793.name: Daniel Chapo
a793.title: President of Mozambique (message conveyed by Maria Lucas)
a793.speech: Asked the minister to convey a welcome to Mozambique to the Chinese special envoy and to inform him that the President is visiting Gaza province and that his 100-day plan was successful because of the support China gave.

a828.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a828.name: John Dramani Mahama
a828.title: President of Ghana
a828.speech: Has called for a major transformation in global health governance, urging African countries to take full control of their healthcare future by designing systems that reflect their own needs, innovations, and priorities, and stressing that Africa must move from being a passive recipient of aid to becoming an active architect of its own health destiny: “Africa must no longer be the patient. It must be the driver, the author, the architect, and the advocate of its own health destiny” ; “The world has changed, but global health governance has not kept pace. This is a moment for us to redesign the architecture that has, for far too long, excluded Africa’s voices, needs, and innovations.”

a828.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a828.name: John Dramani Mahama
a828.title: President of Ghana
a828.speech: Noted that while Africa has made significant progress in child and maternal health, access to medicines, and expanded health coverage through partnerships, those gains are now under threat: “In 2023, development assistance declined sharply, and Africa felt the shock immediately. Maternal health programmes were halted, vaccine supplies delayed, and essential medicines disappeared from shelves. In Ghana, our CHPS compounds were brought to their knees”; emphasized that this was not just a funding issue but a “crisis of imagination” and a “failure of shared responsibility”, and warned that without urgent reforms health systems across Africa would continue to struggle.

a828.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a828.name: John Dramani Mahama
a828.title: President of Ghana
a828.speech: Reminded the summit that African leadership has historically played key roles in global health responses: “Let us remember, when HIV ravaged our continent, it was African leaders who catalysed the response. During Ebola, leaders in West Africa became the moral compass of the world. And during COVID-19, Africa stood up and demanded vaccine justice.”

a828.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a828.name: John Dramani Mahama
a828.title: President of Ghana
a828.speech: Announced the launch of MahamaCare, a sovereign health innovation fund to tackle chronic diseases like hypertension, diabetes, and kidney failure, and shared the story of Acacia, a young mother in Odumase who survived childbirth complications thanks to a digitally linked CHPS compound: “This is not a vision of the future; it is our present reality. We are not only reacting to emergencies, we are building systems that create jobs, reduce inequalities, and uphold human dignity”; also unveiled a high-level task force on global health governance and the SUSTAIN Initiative, an African-led platform to align national budgets with health priorities, attract sovereign and philanthropic investment, and promote accountability.

a828.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a828.name: John Dramani Mahama
a828.title: President of Ghana
a828.speech: Called on African finance ministers and development partners to treat health as a capital investment rather than a cost: “Health is the engine of productivity. It is the currency of our dignity. It is our greatest public good” ; “We must reject the outdated notion that health drains our economies.”

a828.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a828.name: John Dramani Mahama
a828.title: President of Ghana
a828.speech: Concluded his address with a call to action: “Africa’s pain is not a deficit; it is a death of perspective. Our healing is not a plea, it is a rallying cry for sovereignty. Let us reset the moral compass of global health and own our future. From Accra, let the world hear us: let Africa rise.”

a828.speaker: World Health Organization (data cited)
a828.name: World Health Organization (data cited)
a828.speech: Data showing that every dollar invested in health yields up to four dollars in productivity.

a986.speaker: Masaka court (charge sheet read in court)
a986.name: Masaka court (charge sheet read in court)
a986.speech: Read four charges to Lwengo District Chairman Ibrahim Kitatta, including theft and attempted murder, which he is alleged to have committed during the recent NRM primary elections in July.

a986.speaker: Mariam Njuki, lead prosecutor
a986.name: Mariam Njuki
a986.title: lead prosecutor
a986.speech: The prosecution alleges it has evidence incriminating him, and she wanted him remanded so that he would not interfere with the investigations.

a986.speaker: Simon Ntoroko, magistrate of the chief magistrate's court in Masaka
a986.name: Simon Ntoroko
a986.title: magistrate of the chief magistrate's court in Masaka
a986.speech: Rejected the prosecution's request and allowed Kitatta to go free on bail while the case proceeds.

a1018.speaker: Zimbabwe National Chamber of Commerce (ZNCC) 2024 Annual State of Industry and Commerce Survey
a1018.name: Zimbabwe National Chamber of Commerce (ZNCC) 2024 Annual State of Industry and Commerce Survey
a1018.speech: According to the survey, Zimbabwe's tertiary institutions produce approximately 30,000 graduates annually, yet less than 20 per cent are absorbed into the formal job market, leaving thousands to seek alternative livelihoods.

a1018.speaker: UN Population Fund
a1018.name: UN Population Fund
a1018.speech: According to the UN Population Fund, by 2030 nearly five billion people will live in cities, mostly in Africa and Asia, making informal economies central to urban survival and inclusive development.

a1018.speaker: Precious Shumba, director, Harare Residents Trust
a1018.name: Precious Shumba
a1018.title: director, Harare Residents Trust
a1018.speech: "In Zimbabwe, the informal economy is really the engine of a lot of economic growth."

a1018.speaker: Government of Zimbabwe, National Development Strategy 1 (2021-25)
a1018.name: Government of Zimbabwe
a1018.title: National Development Strategy 1 (2021-25)
a1018.speech: Acknowledges the economy's structural regression, marked by de-industrialisation and informalisation.

a1018.speaker: Women informal traders interviewed by New Ziana (unnamed)
a1018.name: Women informal traders interviewed by New Ziana (unnamed)
a1018.speech: Described the informal economy as a "nut that hadn't yet been cracked."

a1018.speaker: Tafadzwa Nyoni, marketing graduate and Indrive taxi driver, Borrowdale, Harare
a1018.name: Tafadzwa Nyoni
a1018.title: marketing graduate and Indrive taxi driver, Borrowdale, Harare

a1018.speaker: Chenai Mudzamiri, vendor from Mutare
a1018.name: Chenai Mudzamiri
a1018.title: vendor from Mutare
a1018.speech: "I wake up at 4am, buy stock from the farms, and sell all day."

a1018.speaker: Bhekimpilo Sibanda, vendor from Makokoba, Bulawayo
a1018.name: Bhekimpilo Sibanda
a1018.title: vendor from Makokoba, Bulawayo
a1018.speech: "When the hardware store I was working in closed, I started selling phone accessories on the pavement."

a1018.speaker: Nomathemba Phiri, vendor from Gweru, Midlands Province
a1018.name: Nomathemba Phiri
a1018.title: vendor from Gweru, Midlands Province
a1018.speech: "I'm vending to pay school fees for my two children. My husband left for South Africa and hasn't been in touch."

a1018.speaker: Emmerson Mnangagwa, President of Zimbabwe
a1018.name: Emmerson Mnangagwa
a1018.title: President of Zimbabwe
a1018.speech: Declared the Glen View Area 8 Home Industry Complex site a state of disaster after the July 2025 fire, unlocking emergency resources and fast-tracking reconstruction.

a1018.speaker: Traders near Makoni Shopping Centre and C-Junction, Chitungwiza (unnamed)
a1018.name: Traders near Makoni Shopping Centre and C-Junction
a1018.title: Chitungwiza (unnamed)
a1018.speech: Reported losing merchandise during the municipality's 2025 enforcement of prohibition and demolition orders; some said their stock was never officially recorded, raising concerns about transparency.

a1018.speaker: Nkosilathi Dube, vendor in Victoria Falls
a1018.name: Nkosilathi Dube
a1018.title: vendor in Victoria Falls
a1018.speech: "We try to sell crafts, fruit, even airtime. But when council officers come, they chase us away, sometimes violently."

a1018.speaker: Research from the University of Zimbabwe's Department of Rural and Urban Planning
a1018.name: Research from the University of Zimbabwe's Department of Rural and Urban Planning
a1018.speech: Shows that informal economies, especially street vending, play a vital role in sustaining livelihoods, particularly for women and youth.

a1018.speaker: Professor Innocent Chirisa and Joel Chaeruka, urban planning experts
a1018.name: Professor Innocent Chirisa and Joel Chaeruka
a1018.title: urban planning experts
a1018.speech: Advocate for zoning reforms, inclusive licensing, and participatory planning.

a1018.speaker: Ministry of Local Government (Zimbabwe)
a1018.name: Ministry of Local Government (Zimbabwe)
a1018.speech: In March 2025 instructed councils to clear illegal vending sites within 48 hours, citing sanitation and congestion concerns.

a1018.speaker: Daniel Garwe, Minister of Local Government
a1018.name: Daniel Garwe
a1018.title: Minister of Local Government
a1018.speech: Emphasised the need for designated spaces with toilets, water points, and security.

a1018.speaker: Samuel Wadzai, Director, Vendors Initiative for Social and Economic Transformation (VISET)
a1018.name: Samuel Wadzai
a1018.title: Director, Vendors Initiative for Social and Economic Transformation (VISET)
a1018.speech: Believes reform must begin by recognising vendors as central to Zimbabwe's urban economy: "Street vendors are a vital part of Zimbabwe's urban economy and livelihoods, and policy must recognise that reality."

a1018.speaker: Samuel Wadzai, Director, Vendors Initiative for Social and Economic Transformation (VISET)
a1018.name: Samuel Wadzai
a1018.title: Director, Vendors Initiative for Social and Economic Transformation (VISET)
a1018.speech: Outlined practical steps: simplify registration and licensing; provide well-serviced trading spaces; ensure access to microfinance and digital payments; and develop policies in genuine partnership with vendor associations; stressed gender sensitivity and scalable, evidence-based interventions.

a1055.speaker: World Health Organisation (WHO)
a1055.name: World Health Organisation (WHO)
a1055.speech: Has warned that the United States' decision to halt foreign aid has "substantially disrupted" the supply of HIV treatments in eight countries, including Nigeria.

a1055.speaker: Tedros Ghebreyesus, WHO Director-General
a1055.name: Tedros Ghebreyesus
a1055.title: WHO Director-General
a1055.speech: Said during a press conference on Monday that the countries - which include Haiti, Kenya, Lesotho, South Sudan, Burkina Faso, Mali, Nigeria, and Ukraine - could soon run out of these life-saving medicines; said the decision has caused disruptions to HIV programmes and put millions of lives at risk: "The disruptions to HIV programnes could undo 20 years of progress"; warned that this setback could lead to over 10 million new HIV cases and three million HIV-related deaths; noted that efforts to tackle HIV, polio, malaria and tuberculosis have been impacted by the US foreign aid pause implemented by President Donald Trump shortly after he assumed office in January.

a1055.speaker: Tedros Ghebreyesus, WHO Director-General
a1055.name: Tedros Ghebreyesus
a1055.title: WHO Director-General
a1055.speech: Highlighted the impact on TB programmes, with 27 countries in Africa and Asia facing significant disruptions, said these include shortages of healthcare workers, diagnostic tools, and collapsing data systems, and noted that nine countries have already reported problems with the procurement and supply chains for TB drugs, threatening the lives of affected individuals: "Over the past two decades, US support for TB services has saved nearly 80 million lives, but this progress is now at risk."

a1055.speaker: Tedros Ghebreyesus, WHO Director-General
a1055.name: Tedros Ghebreyesus
a1055.title: WHO Director-General
a1055.speech: Noted that the US has a "responsibility to ensure that if it withdraws direct funding for countries, it's done in an orderly and humane way that allows them to find alternative sources of funding."

a1055.speaker: Nigerian government (through the National Agency for the Control of AIDS, NACA)
a1055.name: Nigerian government (through the National Agency for the Control of AIDS
a1055.title: NACA)
a1055.speech: Announced plans to strengthen its domestic HIV response two days after Mr Trump's directive, a stance that remained even after the US granted a waiver for HIV intervention, and announced plans to locally produce HIV-related medical tools, including test kits and antiretroviral drugs.

a1055.speaker: Wale Edun, Nigerian Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy
a1055.name: Wale Edun
a1055.title: Nigerian Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy
a1055.speech: According to him, the Federal Executive Council on 3 February approved $1.07 billion to finance healthcare sector reforms under the Human Capital Opportunities for Prosperity and Equity (HOPE) programme, and also approved N4.8 billion for HIV treatment.

a1055.speaker: World Health Organisation (WHO) (separate statement issued on Monday)
a1055.name: World Health Organisation (WHO) (separate statement issued on Monday)
a1055.speech: Said funding shortages could also force 80 per cent of WHO-supported essential health care services in Afghanistan to close; the agency said as of 4 March, 167 health facilities had shut down due to funding shortages, cutting off lifesaving medical care to 1.6 million people across 25 provinces, and that without urgent intervention, over 220 more facilities could close by June 2025, leaving an additional 1.8 million Afghans without access to primary health care.

a1202.speaker: Abiy Ahmed, Prime Minister of Ethiopia
a1202.name: Abiy Ahmed
a1202.title: Prime Minister of Ethiopia
a1202.speech: For the last six months, he consistently articulated that the land-locked Ethiopia needs sea access through diplomacy or force. His public discourse extols populism in disguise of the greatness of Ethiopia, often underscored by any means' occupation of strategic ports at the Red Sea.

a1202.speaker: Ethiopian generals (echoing the Prime Minister)
a1202.name: Ethiopian generals (echoing the Prime Minister)
a1202.speech: Notably, the PM's frequent proclamations, echoed by his generals stating, "We are preparing for a new war," suggest a deliberate effort by the Abiy regime to ready its people for a looming conflict.

a1202.speaker: Prof. Mohamed Hassan
a1202.name: Prof. Mohamed Hassan
a1202.speech: As stated by Prof. Mohamed Hassan, Ethiopia's socioeconomic and political conditions are under great stress. For instance, 70% of Amhara and Oromo lands are out of his hands; the economy is a shamble, unemployment and poverty are rising, and the Tegre crisis is unresolved.

a1202.speaker: Confidential documents widely shared on social media platforms
a1202.name: Confidential documents widely shared on social media platforms
a1202.speech: Abiy adheres to the Oromumma ideology to achieve his prophecy, as was revealed in confidential documents widely shared on most social media platforms. The documents' operational strategy includes several crucial components. The final objective of this ideology is to establish a Kush Republic or Great Oromia, which will be achieved by diminishing the influence of Amhara, Tigray, and Eritrea in the first phase... the strategy entails securing Oromia's dominance within Ethiopia's security forces. The cornerstone of this strategy is gaining access to the Red Sea.

a1203.speaker: Luísa Meque, INGD (National Institute for Disaster Risk Management and Reduction) chairperson
a1203.name: Luísa Meque
a1203.title: INGD (National Institute for Disaster Risk Management and Reduction) chairperson
a1203.speech: speaking to reporters after arriving in Malawi on Friday, said the humanitarian assistance is aimed at benefiting those who fled the country as a result of the demonstrations. "The situation that led you to come here is not at all good, when we are being harassed and our houses are being vandalized. The government is concerned, knowing that there are Mozambican brothers here in Malawi. It made an effort to bring this support here to the refugee centre" ; "In this first phase we have rice, flour, beans and salt. We have also brought blankets and mosquito nets. There is security in Morrumbala district and you should think about returning soon", she added.

a1203.speaker: Alexandre Manjate, Mozambican High Commissioner in Malawi
a1203.name: Alexandre Manjate
a1203.title: Mozambican High Commissioner in Malawi
a1203.speech: also called on the refugees to prepare to return to their areas of origin, "since there is no more insecurity".

a1203.speaker: Venâncio Mondlane, former presidential candidate
a1203.name: Venâncio Mondlane
a1203.title: former presidential candidate
a1203.speech: called mass demonstrations in order to protest against the fraudulent results of the general elections held last October.

a1236.speaker: Millennium Challenge Account Benin (MCA-Benin)
a1236.name: Millennium Challenge Account Benin (MCA-Benin)
a1236.speech: said the handover of these assets bears witness to the mutual will between Benin and the United States of America to shape the electricity sub-sector sustainably; said it had also “ensured rigorous monitoring of the land acquisition process in accordance with the provisions of the Land Code”, and that the vehicles were handed over with a view to “qualitatively improving service to consumers thanks to optimised mobility, better quality supervision and diligent monitoring of operations on the network”.

a1236.speaker: Joël Akowanou, director of operations, MCA-Benin II
a1236.name: Joël Akowanou
a1236.title: director of operations, MCA-Benin II
a1236.speech: said the gesture of MCA-Benin II is nothing more than the keeping of a commitment and a promise; stressed that Benin’s energy transition is under way and will continue given the investment made in the sector thanks to the programme, and that the rolling stock comes at just the right time to help the company in charge of energy in Benin continue to respond favourably to the needs and expectations of the population.

a1236.speaker: Edwige Adohozin Hountondji, secretary general of the Beninese Electricity Company (Sbee)
a1236.name: Edwige Adohozin Hountondji
a1236.title: secretary general of the Beninese Electricity Company (Sbee)
a1236.speech: maintains that these vehicles will enable the company to improve the quality of service and to be closer to customers, and that they will relieve the technical team and facilitate repair operations for subscribers; revealed that the company faces a glaring lack of rolling stock, which has consequences for the quality of service because of delays in dealing with breakdowns and other incidents on the network; said many centres “do not have vehicles for the various interventions” and that “some officials sometimes use their own motorcycles or vehicles to respond to customers’ concerns in the field” ; admitted “With the company’s current challenges, our vehicle fleet is very heavily in demand to respond to customers’ requests and this gem gives us a sigh of relief.”

a1236.speaker: Christopher Broughton, resident director of the Millennium Challenge Corporation in Benin (MCC)
a1236.name: Christopher Broughton
a1236.title: resident director of the Millennium Challenge Corporation in Benin (MCC)
a1236.speech: appreciates the gains drawn by Benin from the programme as a whole and assures that the ambition to strengthen the energy sector with the final objective of reducing poverty through economic growth will be achieved; recalled strong acts of its implementation such as the acquisition of 147 hectares of land at Bohicon, Parakou, Djougou and Natitingou to house four photovoltaic solar power plants with a capacity of 50 megawatts, roughly 18% of national electricity demand during the day; assures that these solar plants will be built through private investors and will produce electricity at a much cheaper cost than production by thermal power plants.

a1236.speaker: Alastaire Sèna Alinsato, representative of the president of the Administration Committee of MCA-Benin II
a1236.name: Alastaire Sèna Alinsato
a1236.title: representative of the president of the Administration Committee of MCA-Benin II
a1236.speech: thanked the United States of America for their support to the efforts of the Beninese government with a view to the efficient availability of electric power; admits the donation of these vehicles and land titles is the symbol of the frank collaboration between the two parties, and said these donations constitute the materialisation of the commitment of the American government and people alongside the national energy bodies.

a1260.speaker: United States Agency for International Development (USAID) (announcement)
a1260.name: United States Agency for International Development (USAID) (announcement)
a1260.speech: USAID recently concluded its Mulu Most At Risk Populations Project to combat HIV/AIDS in Ethiopia and is announcing the launch of a new follow-on project, HIV Services for Key and Priority Populations Activity, a new five-year activity that, through community-based clinical services and public laboratory facilities, will continue to improve HIV testing, link people to HIV treatment, and track viral load suppression, aiming to help Ethiopia reach the UNAIDS and PEPFAR 90-90-90 goal by 2020.

a1301.speaker: OPEC Secretariat (calculations)
a1301.name: OPEC Secretariat (calculations)
a1301.speech: According to OPEC Secretariat calculations, the price of the OPEC basket of 12 crudes stood at $72.38 a barrel on Tuesday, March 5, 2025, compared with $74.98 the previous day.

a1330.speaker: Steadright Critical Minerals Inc. (Canadian mining company)
a1330.name: Steadright Critical Minerals Inc. (Canadian mining company)
a1330.speech: Announced on Thursday the signing of a memorandum of understanding with the shareholders of NSM Capital, a Moroccan company holding mining exploration permits in the Cap Juby region in southern Morocco, an agreement that could lead to an 80% stake in the TitanBeach Titanium project.

a1330.speaker: Steadright Critical Minerals Inc. (Canadian mining company)
a1330.name: Steadright Critical Minerals Inc. (Canadian mining company)
a1330.speech: Said that additional analyses are under way to confirm the 2023 historical sampling data (grades of 42% iron and 4.7% titanium) and to deepen the geological understanding of the site.

a1330.speaker: Matt Lewis, Chief Executive Officer of Steadright
a1330.name: Matt Lewis
a1330.title: Chief Executive Officer of Steadright
a1330.speech: Hailed "the remarkable potential of the TitanBeach sands" and praised the Moroccan mining framework as "conducive to investment, with a tax exemption on profits during the first five years of production."

a1429.speaker: Lazarus Chakwera, President of Malawi
a1429.name: Lazarus Chakwera
a1429.title: President of Malawi
a1429.speech: Has called on Malawians to support the Malawi Red Cross Society (MRCS) in its efforts to raise K200 million for humanitarian activities; speaking during the launch of the MRCS 2025 Flag Week at Kamuzu Palace in Lilongwe, emphasized the importance of uniting to help and support the society, particularly in responding to natural disasters that can affect anyone regardless of their status: "Natural disasters can affect anyone without considering their status, hence we must unite to help and support MRCS as it plays a crucial role in responding to disasters."

a1429.speaker: Khumbize Kandodo Chiponda, Minister of Health of Malawi
a1429.name: Khumbize Kandodo Chiponda
a1429.title: Minister of Health of Malawi
a1429.speech: Echoed the President's sentiments, calling for more support for MRCS: "MRCS is a reliable partner to the nation during national disasters, including cyclones, floods, and others. We must continue to support the society in its efforts to provide humanitarian assistance to those in need."

a1429.speaker: Innocent Majiya, President of the Malawi Red Cross Society (MRCS)
a1429.name: Innocent Majiya
a1429.title: President of the Malawi Red Cross Society (MRCS)
a1429.speech: Explained that the money collected during the Flag Week will be used in various emergency operations in the country: "The funds raised will enable us to respond to emergencies and provide critical support to those affected by disasters."

a1829.speaker: 2016 Global Sustainable Investment Review (report)
a1829.name: 2016 Global Sustainable Investment Review (report)
a1829.speech: Reported that $22.89 trillion worth of assets were "being professionally managed under responsible investment strategies" worldwide, up 25% from 2014, with Europe accounting for $12 trillion and the US total at $8.7 trillion, though the highest growth rates were in Japan and Oceania.

a1829.speaker: Gianni Betti, Costanza Consolandi and Robert G. Eccles (recent paper)
a1829.name: Gianni Betti
a1829.title: Costanza Consolandi and Robert G. Eccles (recent paper)
a1829.speech: Map the relevant ESG issues identified by the Sustainability Accounting Standards Board (SASB) in 79 industries in ten sectors, grouped by SDGs.

a1829.speaker: Mozaffar Khan, George Serafeim and Aaron Yoon (2016 study)
a1829.name: Mozaffar Khan
a1829.title: George Serafeim and Aaron Yoon (2016 study)
a1829.speech: Created portfolios of companies that were performing well and poorly on the material issues in their industry; found the firms with the highest annualized active return (alpha) of 4.8% were performing well on the material issues and poorly on the immaterial issues, while those with the lowest alpha, -2.2%, were performing poorly on both, and that the divergences did not start to appear until after 7-8 years.

a1829.speaker: Mahmoud Mohieldin, World Bank Group Senior Vice President for the 2030 Development Agenda, and Svetlana Klimenko, Lead Financial Management Specialist at the World Bank Group (op-ed authors)
a1829.name: Mahmoud Mohieldin
a1829.title: World Bank Group Senior Vice President for the 2030 Development Agenda, and Svetlana Klimenko, Lead Financial Management Specialist at the World Bank Group (op-ed authors)
a1829.speech: Argue that the annual funding gap for the Sustainable Development Goals is many trillions of dollars and that the only way to close that gap is with the help of the private sector — in particular, by impelling companies to account in their decision-making for environmental, social, and governance issues relevant to the SDGs.

a1903.speaker: Luther Jeke, CEO of iCampus Liberia
a1903.name: Luther Jeke
a1903.title: CEO of iCampus Liberia
a1903.speech: According to Luther Jeke, the initiative, launched in partnership with USAID Liberia through the Feed The Future Initiative and USAID Africa Trade & Investment (ATI) in partnership with Educare Liberia and TRIBE Liberia, has made significant strides since its inception just a year ago.

a1903.speaker: Luther Jeke, CEO of iCampus Liberia
a1903.name: Luther Jeke
a1903.title: CEO of iCampus Liberia
a1903.speech: Expressed optimism about the program's impact, emphasizing its role in providing more than just financial support: "These businesses are equipped with solid, marketable concepts that have matured significantly over the past six to seven months" ; "Our goal is not just to fund these ventures but to foster sustainable growth that contributes to Liberia's economic development."

a1903.speaker: Luther Jeke, CEO of iCampus Liberia
a1903.name: Luther Jeke
a1903.title: CEO of iCampus Liberia
a1903.speech: Highlighted the transformative journey of many participants, who joined the program with limited business management experience but showcased remarkable potential and passion ; underscored the incubator's mission to inspire entrepreneurs to employ young Liberians, empower women, and include persons with disabilities in their operations ; stressed the need to scale the program to reach more businesses across Liberia, leveraging lessons learned to amplify its impact.

a1903.speaker: Luther Jeke, CEO of iCampus Liberia
a1903.name: Luther Jeke
a1903.title: CEO of iCampus Liberia
a1903.speech: "Global statistics show that 90% of small businesses fail within their first year. However, we're proud to report that 80% of our participants are thriving — a testament to the effectiveness of the coaching, mentoring, and guidance we provide."

a1903.speaker: Luther Jeke, CEO of iCampus Liberia
a1903.name: Luther Jeke
a1903.title: CEO of iCampus Liberia
a1903.speech: "Entrepreneurship is not just about profits — it's about creating opportunities, solving problems, and building a better future for our communities."

a1903.speaker: Panel of five judges at the Pitch Competition Event
a1903.name: Panel of five judges at the Pitch Competition Event
a1903.speech: Applauded the ingenuity and determination displayed throughout the event.

a1903.speaker: Cllr. Margaret Nigba, CEO of Her Voice Agriculture Farm Limited
a1903.name: Cllr. Margaret Nigba
a1903.title: CEO of Her Voice Agriculture Farm Limited
a1903.speech: "Our aim is to make honey accessible to everyone in our community. With this grant, we plan to purchase a liquid filling machine that will allow us to produce high-quality honey at a price of just L$50 in local shops."

a1903.speaker: Cllr. Margaret Nigba, CEO of Her Voice Agriculture Farm Limited
a1903.name: Cllr. Margaret Nigba
a1903.title: CEO of Her Voice Agriculture Farm Limited
a1903.speech: Reflecting on the competitive nature of the event, said, "The nine competitors in my category were exceptionally talented, presenting innovative ideas. Emerging as one of the top three finalists is a testament to the hard work of my entire team." ; credited her team's dedication for the achievement and expressed confidence in her business's future: "This win is not just about me; it's about the team that made it possible. We're committed to demonstrating our responsibility and delivering on our promises."

a1903.speaker: Miamiatta-Fatima Kroma, CEO of Royal Farm, Grand Cape Mount
a1903.name: Miamiatta-Fatima Kroma
a1903.title: CEO of Royal Farm, Grand Cape Mount
a1903.speech: "Liberia has the capacity to produce enough food to sustain our population. It's disheartening that we rely so heavily on imports for basic necessities. My goal is to provide healthier, locally produced alternatives." ; emphasized the advantages of South African and East African goat breeds over traditional West African goats: "These breeds produce more meat while maintaining the same price point—$5 per pound. Our plan is to package and distribute these products in local supermarkets."

a1903.speaker: Miamiatta-Fatima Kroma, CEO of Royal Farm, Grand Cape Mount
a1903.name: Miamiatta-Fatima Kroma
a1903.title: CEO of Royal Farm, Grand Cape Mount
a1903.speech: "Seeing people constantly asking for help broke my heart. I wanted to empower them with skills and opportunities to earn a decent living."

a1903.speaker: Megan Kyles, Director, Economic Growth, USAID-Liberia
a1903.name: Megan Kyles
a1903.title: Director, Economic Growth, USAID-Liberia
a1903.speech: Reminded the recipients of the grant of their roles in driving the Liberian economy: "What drives the economy is you, the (Business People) and as such you are expected to use the grant for the purpose for which it is intended. Expand your business so that it serves as encouragement for others in your community." ; encouraged grantees to go into their respective communities and be able to impact others as their businesses expand.

a1922.speaker: Elon Musk, tech billionaire / head of the Department of Government Efficiency
a1922.name: Elon Musk
a1922.title: tech billionaire / head of the Department of Government Efficiency
a1922.speech: revealed that the US government accidentally cut Ebola virus prevention efforts ; told a US Cabinet meeting that the Department of Government Efficiency had made mistakes as it cut jobs and programmes in recent weeks: "We won't be perfect, but when we make mistake, we'll fix it very quickly." ; said one such mistake was "accidentally" cancelling Ebola prevention while cutting US development aid agency USAID ; "I think we all want Ebola prevention. So we restored the Ebola prevention immediately, and there was no interruption."

a1922.speaker: Elon Musk, tech billionaire / head of the Department of Government Efficiency
a1922.name: Elon Musk
a1922.title: tech billionaire / head of the Department of Government Efficiency
a1922.speech: "But we do need to move quickly if we are to achieve a trillion-dollar deficit reduction in financial year 2026. It requires saving 4 billion dollars per day, every day, from now through the end of September. But we can do it, and we will do it."

a1927.speaker: David M. Farhat, former Liberian Finance Minister
a1927.name: David M. Farhat
a1927.title: former Liberian Finance Minister
a1927.speech: Welcomes U.S. President Donald Trump's recent decision to impose a 90-day moratorium on funding and aid programs globally, including those in Africa; emphasizes that these moves by the U.S. Government are aimed at prompting African leaders to enhance their leadership roles and improve citizens' livelihoods across the continent ; "For over a century, the United States has played a crucial role in supporting Liberia's hospitals, schools, and various government programs to help move the country forward," ; "However, I believe it is time for our leaders to take responsibility and make better use of the resources that God has blessed our continent with."

a1927.speaker: David M. Farhat, former Liberian Finance Minister
a1927.name: David M. Farhat
a1927.title: former Liberian Finance Minister
a1927.speech: Commended President Joseph N. Boakai for cutting benefits to certain directors and board members in his administration.

a1927.speaker: David M. Farhat, former Liberian Finance Minister
a1927.name: David M. Farhat
a1927.title: former Liberian Finance Minister
a1927.speech: Said he never earned more than US$2,000 as a monthly salary, but notes that today, some individuals take home over US$15,000, while children and parents beg in street corners for basic necessities; says despite Liberia being rich in natural resources, years of poor governance have resulted in widespread poverty among the populace.

a1927.speaker: David M. Farhat, former Liberian Finance Minister
a1927.name: David M. Farhat
a1927.title: former Liberian Finance Minister
a1927.speech: Encourages President Boakai to take further action, highlighting that many Liberians struggle daily to make ends meet: "The President must utilize this challenging period to realign our economy," he urges, suggesting a comprehensive review of concession agreements in the country; advocates for standardization, realignment, and restructuring of these agreements to ensure fairness and maximize benefits for Liberians.

a1927.speaker: David M. Farhat, former Liberian Finance Minister
a1927.name: David M. Farhat
a1927.title: former Liberian Finance Minister
a1927.speech: Expresses gratitude to Nimba County District #7 Representative Musa Bility for proposing a 50% reduction in salaries and benefits for all legislators, including Senators and Representatives; clarifies that he does not support the ongoing power struggle in the 55th Legislature but backs Bility's proposal for the common good of the country, emphasizing that stagnation seen in Liberia and elsewhere on the continent arises from leaders who prioritize personal gains over the welfare of the people.

a1927.speaker: Musa Bility, Nimba County District #7 Representative
a1927.name: Musa Bility
a1927.title: Nimba County District #7 Representative
a1927.speech: proposing a 50% reduction in salaries and benefits for all legislators, including Senators and Representatives, as a measure to address the nation's challenges.

a1935.speaker: Center for Global Development (CGD) (analysis based on data presented to the US Congress on 27 March)
a1935.name: Center for Global Development (CGD) (analysis based on data presented to the US Congress on 27 March)
a1935.speech: Assessed, on the basis of the data presented to the US Congress on 27 March, how much American aid different countries of the world have lost - in addition to the absolute amounts and the share of total USAID funding, the experts evaluated the losses to each recipient country's GNI.

a1935.speaker: The Africa Report
a1935.name: The Africa Report
a1935.speech: Systematised the CGD data by African country, showing losses including Ethiopia $386.9 million (30% of USAID funding, 0.24% of GNI), DR Congo $386.7 million (34%, 0.6%), Uganda $306.8 million (66%, 0.64%), South Africa $260.6 million (89%, 0.07%), Kenya $224.7 million (46%, 0.21%), Liberia $102.7 million (98%, 2.59%) and others; nine countries lost USAID aid entirely, and Liberia, whose funding was cut by 98%, will lose a significant share of GNI (2.59%), having been one of the continent's most aid-dependent countries.

a1946.speaker: Ousmane Diagana, Vice-President of the World Bank, West and Central Africa
a1946.name: Ousmane Diagana
a1946.title: Vice-President of the World Bank, West and Central Africa
a1946.speech: Has hailed the spiralling impact of the Gulf of Guinea Northern Regions Social Cohesion Project (SOCO) on the lives of people, especially those in poor rural communities in northern Ghana. “SOCO”, he noted, “is a game changer”, and gave assurance of expediting action for the release of funds to continue the project and also increase the beneficiary communities. ; “I am very satisfied. I have seen concrete activities that have been funded by the project. I am very impressed to see that there is a community at large that is a beneficiary of the project – that is the essence of the project. They consider it their project – so there is this sense of community ownership, which is critical.” ; “I also understand that this is a need that was expressed by the community themselves. So, it means that we have been responsive to their needs. This is what this type of project is supposed to do. Of course, given the magnitude of the need, it will be very important to put to good use what exists already – to have very good communication about what the project activities are so that the partners will be more encouraged to do more.”

a1946.speaker: Ousmane Diagana, Vice-President of the World Bank, West and Central Africa
a1946.name: Ousmane Diagana
a1946.title: Vice-President of the World Bank, West and Central Africa
a1946.speech: Said the numerous requests for the extension of the project to non-beneficiary communities were a sign of the successes of the SOCO project and gave an assurance that the World Bank would continue to support the project to achieve desired results; he was also optimistic that governments in the four beneficiary countries, Ghana, Togo, Benin and La Cote d’Ivoire, would also do their part to ensure the sustainability of the project.

a1946.speaker: Ministry of Local Government, Decentralisation and Rural Development (data released)
a1946.name: Ministry of Local Government
a1946.title: Decentralisation and Rural Development (data released)
a1946.speech: According to data released by the Ministry, farmers who sell their cattle at the Livestock Market, which started operations on November 3, 2024, make an income of about GH¢400,000 each market day on Sundays; income from the sale of small ruminants each market day is also estimated at GH¢100,000.

a1946.speaker: SOCO project implementers
a1946.name: SOCO project implementers
a1946.speech: According to the SOCO project implementers, the investments made in these groups had brought about social cohesion by bringing the people together.

a1946.speaker: Robert Taliercio O’Brien, World Bank Ghana Country Director
a1946.name: Robert Taliercio O’Brien
a1946.title: World Bank Ghana Country Director
a1946.speech: Said feedback from the beneficiary MMDAs was very useful to the bank to understand their need to see how the projects were structured to achieve desired results.

a1946.speaker: Samuel Seth Passah, Director for Local Governance and Decentralisation
a1946.name: Samuel Seth Passah
a1946.title: Director for Local Governance and Decentralisation
a1946.speech: Speaking on behalf of the Chief Director at the engagement with project stakeholders, revealed the interest the SOCO project had attracted among the government and other development partners of the country and highlighted some of the progress made so far: “Within two years of the project’s effectiveness date, we have begun to see its impact on the ground across 48 districts, 217 clusters, covering 1,700 communities, representing a population of 1.5 million. The project has also disbursed US$60 million, which is 40 per cent out of the total US$150 million in the last two years.”

a1946.speaker: Elizabeth Ohenewah Agyei, Coordinator of the SOCO project
a1946.name: Elizabeth Ohenewah Agyei
a1946.title: Coordinator of the SOCO project
a1946.speech: Said one challenging issue her outfit had had to battle with was how to get the minority groups in the community to participate in the project; nevertheless, she said continuous engagement with the minority groupings was yielding positive results, further solidifying the sustainability of the project in the beneficiary communities.

a1946.speaker: Elizabeth Ohenewah Agyei, Coordinator of the SOCO project
a1946.name: Elizabeth Ohenewah Agyei
a1946.title: Coordinator of the SOCO project
a1946.speech: Noted that the project development goals had been achieved within two years of its implementation, anchoring her response on the impact of the project on the lives of the people: “Going forward, we should see how others who are looking forward to being beneficiaries are attended to. One of the things that we also look forward to is being very specific to be able to measure the changes that are occurring. This is because if you are not able to measure the impact that these projects are making, then we won’t be able to know where exactly and how the next step will be.”

a2047.speaker: Chima's younger sister (about four years old)
a2047.name: Chima's younger sister (about four years old)
a2047.speech: "He is hungry," she whispered, her voice barely audible.

a2047.speaker: Chima's eldest brother
a2047.name: Chima's eldest brother
a2047.speech: "My mummy went to buy food."

a2047.speaker: United Nations Children's Fund (UNICEF) report
a2047.name: United Nations Children's Fund (UNICEF) report
a2047.speech: A UNICEF report says that 11 million or one in three Nigerian children under five are experiencing severe food poverty ; UNICEF says eight out of ten Nigerian malnourished children lack access to treatment ; UNICEF data as of 2015 showed only two out of ten malnourished children in Nigeria could access treatment ; approximately 2,400 malnourished children die daily, as compiled by UNICEF.

a2047.speaker: Rose Okafor, Chima's mother, market trader at Ile-Epo market, Lagos
a2047.name: Rose Okafor
a2047.title: Chima's mother, market trader at Ile-Epo market, Lagos
a2047.speech: "This is how we have survived since January 2024, when food became the preserve of rich men," she lamented. "I've been collecting leftovers from any available parties where I disguise myself as a guest. A neighbour showed me this way. I can't watch my child, the little I earn won't buy food in the market," she confessed ; believes "survival matters", as she echoed at different occasions.

a2047.speaker: World Health Organisation (WHO)
a2047.name: World Health Organisation (WHO)
a2047.speech: Recommends that children like Chima receive at least five food groups daily—from breast milk and proteins to fruits and vegetables ; affirms that children under five are disproportionately affected by malnutrition.

a2047.speaker: Good Health Weekly (lifestyle-focused publication) findings
a2047.name: Good Health Weekly (lifestyle-focused publication) findings
a2047.speech: Findings that Nigerians no longer eat for nutrients, but to fill their stomach for energy.

a2047.speaker: Prof. Ekanem Ekure, President of the Paediatric Association of Nigeria (PAN)
a2047.name: Prof. Ekanem Ekure
a2047.title: President of the Paediatric Association of Nigeria (PAN)
a2047.speech: Blamed it on poverty and unaffordable food prices: "This development also threatens to reverse previous gains in childhood survival, likewise obstructs SDG 3 achievement," she stated.

a2047.speaker: Blessing Akombi (Akombi-Inyang), Maternal and Child Health Expert
a2047.name: Blessing Akombi (Akombi-Inyang)
a2047.title: Maternal and Child Health Expert
a2047.speech: Citing consequences of poor nutrition: "Children risk stunted physical and cognitive development, weak immunity, frequent infections, and lifelong effects on education, productivity and health."

a2047.speaker: Rose Okafor, Chima's mother
a2047.name: Rose Okafor
a2047.title: Chima's mother
a2047.speech: On the cost of treatment and therapeutic food: "I rarely make N2,000 daily ($1.31), how am I expected to get money for therapeutic food? Even the recommended local substitutes are beyond my reach, but I still try to give him beans and add some milk to his pap, though not consistently, due to the cost. My husband is just a site labourer who struggles to get engagements, so I expect little or no support from him" ; reported that a physician complained Chima was battling infections and severe malnourishment, and said doctors' dietary advice was unrealistic.

a2047.speaker: Rose Okafor, Chima's mother
a2047.name: Rose Okafor
a2047.title: Chima's mother
a2047.speech: On the family's declining diet: "Before now, we could afford two decent meals a day, with a little spice of protein. I would split one egg among the three of them, but it is now too costly. If I couldn't give Ponmo (cowhide), I'd add Puff Puff for flavour, this too is now on the high side," she recounted ; said that on days when there are no parties to scavenge food, she enters food stores to pick up spilt grains of raw rice and beans.

a2047.speaker: Intelpoint (data platform analysis)
a2047.name: Intelpoint (data platform analysis)
a2047.speech: An analysis by data platform Intelpoint comparing prices of food items between April 2023 and December 2024 showed an increase by up to 353 per cent, far outpacing the prevailing 133 per cent wage increase.

a2047.speaker: Babatunde Ojei, Country Director at the International Rescue Committee (IRC)
a2047.name: Babatunde Ojei
a2047.title: Country Director at the International Rescue Committee (IRC)
a2047.speech: Noted that donors' reluctance and global food aid cuts will likely compound an already precarious situation: "It's heartbreaking to see the needs of children growing while the support to reach them is shrinking. Fewer implementing partners are active, as donor reluctance, driven by insecurity, limited access, and global aid cuts, continue to restrict funding."

a2047.speaker: Queen Praise, daughter of Grace Eseneowo's employer
a2047.name: Queen Praise
a2047.title: daughter of Grace Eseneowo's employer
a2047.speech: Revealed Grace's struggles publicly to solicit support for her and highlight the wider hunger crisis: "She usually saves some feed from my father's farm where she works and prepares same as pap for her children."

a2047.speaker: National Bureau of Statistics (NBS) poverty index of 2023
a2047.name: National Bureau of Statistics (NBS) poverty index of 2023
a2047.speech: Akwa Ibom is ranked 27th of 36 states on the National Bureau of Statistics (NBS) poverty index of 2023.

a2047.speaker: American Chemical Society
a2047.name: American Chemical Society
a2047.speech: Warned that chicken feeds often contain growth enhancing arsenic-based drugs linked to cancer, heart disease, and diabetes in humans.

a2047.speaker: Nma Jiya, consultant paediatrician at Usmanu Danfodiyo University Teaching Hospital, Sokoto
a2047.name: Nma Jiya
a2047.title: consultant paediatrician at Usmanu Danfodiyo University Teaching Hospital, Sokoto
a2047.speech: Said that many more children are being admitted to clinics with causes related to malnutrition; disclosed that about 80–90 percent of paediatric cases in recent times are malnutrition-related, adding that the surge was unprecedented, and worried that the surge was ill-timed given medical brain drain plaguing the health system ; "We're witnessing a historic surge in vaccine-preventable, communicable and non-communicable diseases among children. We've had to deal with several cases of hypoglycemia, hypothermia, excessive coldness, anaemia, liver failure, and electrolyte imbalances, largely due to poor diet."

a2047.speaker: Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF)
a2047.name: Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF)
a2047.speech: Expressed concern about the deteriorating condition of malnourished children in the country, reporting a 74 percent increase in admitted malnourished children to its facility in Kebbi State in the first half of 2025, and more than 100 percent increase across the Northern region: "Not just the children, even mothers accompanying young patients are themselves acutely malnourished."

a2047.speaker: Nma Jiya, consultant paediatrician
a2047.name: Nma Jiya
a2047.title: consultant paediatrician
a2047.speech: Expressed that while the influx coincides with the mass exodus of health workers, ailing children may not get the best: "We're losing doctors and nurses almost every day, while patients keep streaming in. We are facing a crisis. It is even worse in the North, where we face local and International Japa."

a2047.speaker: Nigerian Medical Association (NMA)
a2047.name: Nigerian Medical Association (NMA)
a2047.speech: Reports that at least 50 medical doctors leave the country every week in search of greener pastures abroad over poor working conditions.

a2047.speaker: Dr. Chris Esezobo, Paediatric Nephrologist at the Lagos University Teaching Hospital
a2047.name: Dr. Chris Esezobo
a2047.title: Paediatric Nephrologist at the Lagos University Teaching Hospital
a2047.speech: Flagged Nigeria's low paediatrician-to-patient ratio, warning that the gap is attracting incompetent child specialists and is a contributor to deaths of approximately 2,400 malnourished children daily: "Some states have no paediatricians. Some local government areas in Lagos lack paediatric doctors. Children in Nigeria are dying due to a lack of skilled manpower."

a2047.speaker: Prof. Ekanem Ekure, President of PAN and Consultant at Lagos State University Teaching Hospital
a2047.name: Prof. Ekanem Ekure
a2047.title: President of PAN and Consultant at Lagos State University Teaching Hospital
a2047.speech: Findings with PAN's President, Ekure, revealed that the issues stem from poor diet and hygiene: "Although not as severe as Northern states, hospital admissions of children have somewhat increased in the South West due to malnutrition. This remains a serious concern with multiple underlying causes."

a2047.speaker: A relative of a bereaved mother (name unknown)
a2047.name: A relative of a bereaved mother (name unknown)
a2047.speech: "She had just lost her two-year-old child to anaemia."

a2047.speaker: A doctor at Orile Agege General Hospital (unnamed, without a name tag)
a2047.name: A doctor at Orile Agege General Hospital (unnamed
a2047.title: without a name tag)
a2047.speech: "Next patient, please," the doctor called.

a2047.speaker: Rose Okafor, Chima's mother
a2047.name: Rose Okafor
a2047.title: Chima's mother
a2047.speech: On being ignored at the hospital: "This is my fourth visit this week. I've only seen doctor once. They'll probably ignore us again," she wept.

a2047.speaker: Rose Okafor, Chima's mother
a2047.name: Rose Okafor
a2047.title: Chima's mother
a2047.speech: On Chima's worsening condition and care: "Today, he has malaria. Tomorrow, he is stooling, every time, it is always one infection or the other, but they keep saying he is not eating well. I've been trying in my capacity, yet, his condition is not improving. His mates are already crawling, but he doesn't show any sign yet. Some people are suggesting herbal treatment, I'm afraid it may even compound his situation. I've been coming here every other day for three months now, but his condition only worsens. The health workers already know us, so they ignore us or attend to us hastily. They tell me they're short-staffed and have many children to treat. At times, they will say I should continue with old medications even when I have new complaints. I'm tired, I just want him to be well. His condition has drained us. The little help we get goes on drugs and tests. He has been placed on special diets, including infant formula and vitamin C. I still try to give him vitamin C, but could not sustain other recommended because of the cost," she grieved.

a2047.speaker: International Rescue Committee (IRC)
a2047.name: International Rescue Committee (IRC)
a2047.speech: Reported that more than four out of five children suffering from nutritional ailments are denied life-saving treatment due to lack of funds and bureaucracy ; recently declared an outrageous number of severely malnourished children admitted to its clinic, with cases surging by 178 percent between March and July 2025.

a2047.speaker: Dr. Simba Tirima, immediate Past Country Representative of MSF
a2047.name: Dr. Simba Tirima
a2047.title: immediate Past Country Representative of MSF
a2047.speech: Once reacting to this dilemma in the previous year, said: "We are resorting to treating patients on mattresses on the floor because our facilities are full."

a2047.speaker: Ahmed Aldikhari, Country Representative of MSF
a2047.name: Ahmed Aldikhari
a2047.title: Country Representative of MSF
a2047.speech: Bemoaned an escalating toll, noting that over 652 malnourished children have died in its Katsina facilities this year alone: "They couldn't get timely access to care," he worried.

a2047.speaker: Mrs Yewande Gansallo, paediatric nurse at Bola Ahmed Tinubu Health Centre, Aboru, Lagos
a2047.name: Mrs Yewande Gansallo
a2047.title: paediatric nurse at Bola Ahmed Tinubu Health Centre, Aboru, Lagos
a2047.speech: Observed a trend of recurring illnesses, mostly infections, among children visiting the clinic, wondering why such is prevalent: "They keep coming back with the same complaints every week, and we keep treating the same condition repeatedly. It's so strange."

a2047.speaker: Nma Jiya, consultant paediatrician
a2047.name: Nma Jiya
a2047.title: consultant paediatrician
a2047.speech: Remarked that Gansallo's concern is not uncommon among malnourished children, adding that such is very likely when their immune systems are already compromised by prolonged nutritional deficiencies ; "The ongoing wave of brain drain couldn't have come at a worse time," he lamented. "Unfortunately, those who suffer most, as we often see them, are children from low-income families. They can barely afford good food or a private consultation."

a2047.speaker: Kashim Shettima, Vice President of Nigeria
a2047.name: Kashim Shettima
a2047.title: Vice President of Nigeria
a2047.speech: Once admitting the cost of malnutrition, said: "This remains a national emergency that poses both health and security threats to Nigeria. At one point, the Ministry of Agriculture and Food Security proposed a nationwide prayer & fasting in response to the escalating situation, a move widely dismissed as unserious."

a2047.speaker: Dr. David Adewole, public health expert
a2047.name: Dr. David Adewole
a2047.title: public health expert
a2047.speech: "This policy may not do much. As much as it may be good, its proper implementation and sustainability might be a challenge due to the government's habit of policy somersaults."

a2047.speaker: Babajide Saheed, Chairperson of the Lagos NMA chapter (statement issued on Workers' Day 2025)
a2047.name: Babajide Saheed
a2047.title: Chairperson of the Lagos NMA chapter (statement issued on Workers' Day 2025)
a2047.speech: Stressed the urgency of addressing the 'japa' dilemma, noting delays in implementing policies on health workforce migration, and called for better remuneration, including non-taxable call duty allowances and professional allowances indexed to the national inflation rate: "Better welfare packages, including affordable housing and car loans, and adopting the CONMESS salary structure while ending exploitative locum appointments will drive fair pay and career growth."

a2047.speaker: Prof. Ekanem Ekure, President of the Paediatric Association of Nigeria (PAN)
a2047.name: Prof. Ekanem Ekure
a2047.title: President of the Paediatric Association of Nigeria (PAN)
a2047.speech: Expressed belief that children's present plight resulted from non-implementation of the Child Rights Act (CRA), despite its domestication across states, urging governments to intensify their commitment to its enforcement: "CRA guarantees Nigerian children's rights to family life, nutrition, and health. The Federal Government should lead by example and drive its enforcement across states."

a2047.speaker: Blessing Akombi-Inyang, child health expert
a2047.name: Blessing Akombi-Inyang
a2047.title: child health expert
a2047.speech: "Since malnutrition stems from poverty, addressing it requires a multidimensional approach that tackles various deprivations that necessitate a commitment from government at all levels. At household level, efforts should be devoted to promoting good water, sanitation and hygiene, while at the community level, there should be deliberate and consistent move to support underprivileged households in form of food and cash transfers."

a2047.speaker: Prof Mike Ogirima, former Chairman of the Nigerian Medical Association (NMA)
a2047.name: Prof Mike Ogirima
a2047.title: former Chairman of the Nigerian Medical Association (NMA)
a2047.speech: Advised on the need to strengthen Primary Healthcare Centres (PHCs) by integrating nutrition counselling, promoting exclusive breastfeeding and embracing local food supplements like soya beans.

a2047.speaker: Mrs. Blessing Olugbemi, a farmer
a2047.name: Mrs. Blessing Olugbemi
a2047.title: a farmer
a2047.speech: Urged mothers to consider affordable, protein-rich alternatives instead of abandoning them altogether due to high costs: "Crayfish, Ugu (pumpkin) leaves and herring fish (Sawa) are all nutritious and flavorful cheap options that can be added to children's meal for optimal health."

a2425.speaker: Atupele Muluzi, UDF leader and Malawian presidential aspirant
a2425.name: Atupele Muluzi
a2425.title: UDF leader and Malawian presidential aspirant
a2425.speech: Declares himself “ripe, equipped, and ready” to lead Malawi in 2025 and promises transformative leadership grounded in a bold economic and social vision, with campaign priorities on food security, energy development, export promotion, education reform and tourism revitalisation ; promises to dismantle the Thangata system, which perpetuates poverty among smallholder farmers, and calls for a Sovereign Wealth Fund ; rejects “savagery politics” and excessive deference to leaders, asking to be called “Mr. President” instead of “His Excellency” ; promises a revitalised UDF and emphasises being clean and inclusive in politics.

a2425.speaker: Atupele Muluzi, UDF leader and Malawian presidential aspirant
a2425.name: Atupele Muluzi
a2425.title: UDF leader and Malawian presidential aspirant
a2425.speech: Acknowledges the perception of dynastic politics, asserting, “I am Atupele, living in my own generation.”

a2425.speaker: Atupele Muluzi, UDF leader and Malawian presidential aspirant
a2425.name: Atupele Muluzi
a2425.title: UDF leader and Malawian presidential aspirant
a2425.speech: Cautions Malawians against voting out of anger.

a2581.speaker: African Union Mission in Somalia (AMISOM) (statement)
a2581.name: African Union Mission in Somalia (AMISOM) (statement)
a2581.speech: expresses its heartfelt condolences to the families of those who perished in the plane crash of 4th May, 2020.

a2581.speaker: Somali Journalists Syndicate (SJS), Federation of Somali Journalists (FESOJ), Somali Media Association (SOMA) and Somali Independent Media Houses Association (SIMHA) (joint statement)
a2581.name: Somali Journalists Syndicate (SJS)
a2581.title: Federation of Somali Journalists (FESOJ), Somali Media Association (SOMA) and Somali Independent Media Houses Association (SIMHA) (joint statement)
a2581.speech: strongly condemn the killing of Kalsan TV journalist, Said Yusuf Ali who was stabbed to death.

a2581.speaker: Somali media fraternity (joint statement)
a2581.name: Somali media fraternity (joint statement)
a2581.speech: vehemently condemns in the strongest terms possible the assault and the injury on female journalist Safiya Aden Osman, a reporter for Shabelle TV and her cameraman, Abdulkadir Ga'al by Waberi District police and District Officials in Mogadishu.

a2581.speaker: Undersigned Somalia media fraternity (World Press Freedom Day statement)
a2581.name: Undersigned Somalia media fraternity (World Press Freedom Day statement)
a2581.speech: express our grave concern on the spate of threats, attacks and intimidation against journalists and media professionals in the past year.

a2581.speaker: United Nations envoy to Somalia
a2581.name: United Nations envoy to Somalia
a2581.speech: called for Somali journalists to be able to perform their work freely, on the occasion of World Press Freedom Day.

a2581.speaker: Somali Journalists Syndicate (SJS)
a2581.name: Somali Journalists Syndicate (SJS)
a2581.speech: wishes all Somali journalists a Happy International Workers' Day.

a2581.speaker: Committee to Protect Journalists (CPJ)
a2581.name: Committee to Protect Journalists (CPJ)
a2581.speech: said Somali authorities should immediately release radio journalist Mohamed Abdiwahab Nuur and allow him to work freely.

a2581.speaker: Somalia Health and Demographic Survey (SHDS) Report 2020
a2581.name: Somalia Health and Demographic Survey (SHDS) Report 2020
a2581.speech: offers the country's decision makers and stakeholders vital information on the health and lives of Somali women of childbearing ages and children.

a2883.speaker: Human Rights Watch (report)
a2883.name: Human Rights Watch (report)
a2883.speech: According to a Human Rights Watch report published today, the Seleka has killed several dozen unarmed civilians and has also taken part in the arbitrary destruction of numerous homes and villages. The 84-page report, entitled "'I Can Still Smell the Dead': The Forgotten Human Rights Crisis in the Central African Republic", describes the deliberate killings of civilians - including women, children and the elderly - between March and June 2013, and confirms the deliberate destruction of more than 1,000 houses in Bangui and in the provinces. Human Rights Watch documented the deaths of a large number of people from wounds, hunger or disease ; documented that the Seleka killed 17 people in the Damala neighbourhood of Bangui on 27 March, that at least 18 civilians were killed on the Ngaragba bridge on 13 April, and that more than 1,000 houses were destroyed in at least 34 villages in the north of the country between February and June ; the report also reports numerous killings of people associated with the army under deposed president Francois Bozize.

a2883.speaker: Human Rights Watch (recommendations)
a2883.name: Human Rights Watch (recommendations)
a2883.speech: According to Human Rights Watch, the Seleka should immediately put an end to the killings and looting, restore order and allow access to humanitarian aid that is desperately lacking. Seleka leaders should control their forces, denounce the killings committed by their members and supporters, restore civil administration throughout the country, and ensure accountability for the crimes committed. International bodies and the countries concerned should help the African Union peacekeeping mission do its work and should impose targeted sanctions against those responsible for human rights abuses, including Seleka leaders.

a2883.speaker: Daniel Bekele, Africa director at Human Rights Watch
a2883.name: Daniel Bekele
a2883.title: Africa director at Human Rights Watch
a2883.speech: "Seleka leaders promised a fresh start for the people of the Central African Republic, but instead they have carried out large-scale attacks against civilians, engaging in looting and killing." "Worse still, the Seleka recruited children, some of them no older than 13, to commit some of these horrific acts." ; "The Seleka may have real grievances against the former regime, but nothing excuses such a level of violence against civilians." "The Seleka seems to be focusing more on acts of looting targeting various layers of the population than on restoring a functioning government that can protect people from abuses."

a2883.speaker: Daniel Bekele, Africa director at Human Rights Watch
a2883.name: Daniel Bekele
a2883.title: Africa director at Human Rights Watch
a2883.speech: "The Central African Republic is truly experiencing an ignored crisis as regards the humanitarian and human rights situation." "Driven from their homes by the Seleka, countless people are living in the bush in tents made from shrubs and leaves, and without access to food or water. They need immediate assistance as well as protection."

a2883.speaker: A witness (anonymous)
a2883.name: A witness (anonymous)
a2883.speech: "[He] went from door to door in the village to ask people to come out of their homes and come to a meeting to talk with the Seleka. The first ones left their houses, five of them, and were gathered under a tree ... they were tied together by the arms. They were then shot one after the other."

a2883.speaker: Survivors of the Mpoko river executions
a2883.name: Survivors of the Mpoko river executions
a2883.speech: The survivors described to Human Rights Watch step by step how they were taken to the river, lined up and prepared for execution until a Seleka member realised that the men had in fact not been soldiers under Bozize and spared those who had not yet been killed.

a2883.speaker: Representatives of the transitional government, including interim president Michel Djotodia
a2883.name: Representatives of the transitional government
a2883.title: including interim president Michel Djotodia
a2883.speech: In interviews with Human Rights Watch, played down the scale of the massacres, claiming that most were the work of "fake Seleka" or of Bozize supporters.

a2883.speaker: Former detainees of the Bossembele military training centre
a2883.name: Former detainees of the Bossembele military training centre
a2883.speech: Detainees told Human Rights Watch that they were held incommunicado and in inhuman conditions for months or years, and that many of them were tortured ; they and other sources explained to Human Rights Watch that Bozize was in the habit of visiting the centre and that he owned a private villa nearby, and reported the cases of at least two men who had been forced to dig holes before being shot and buried by the Presidential Guard.

a2883.speaker: National prosecutor of the Central African Republic
a2883.name: National prosecutor of the Central African Republic
a2883.speech: On 29 May, announced an international arrest warrant against Bozize, who has fled the CAR.

a2883.speaker: Michel Djotodia, interim president of the Central African Republic
a2883.name: Michel Djotodia
a2883.title: interim president of the Central African Republic
a2883.speech: On 13 September, dissolved the Seleka coalition and announced that the official state forces were responsible for security.

a2993.speaker: AA (Automobile Association), South West Africa
a2993.name: AA (Automobile Association)
a2993.title: South West Africa
a2993.speech: As the AA reports this morning, the roads from Windhoek to Walvis Bay via the Gamsberg Pass and the Khomas Highland are closed to traffic. Also closed are the roads from Mariental to Asanib via Witbooisvlei, from Helmeringhausen to Bethanien via Kerkhof, from Feldschuhhorn to Witpütz and from Asanib to Koës. All other sand roads are wet but passable.

a2993.speaker: I. M. Zaayman, Director of Posts and Telecommunications in South West Africa
a2993.name: I. M. Zaayman
a2993.title: Director of Posts and Telecommunications in South West Africa
a2993.speech: Stated that despite the heavy rains, which are still falling, most of the damaged telephone connections have been repaired. Only in the south of the country are several farms cut off from the outside world, because flowing rivers and roads that are in part completely washed away are holding up the repair technicians. ; Patience is requested until all faults have been rectified, the statement says.

a2993.speaker: Church leadership of the DELK (German Evangelical Lutheran Church)
a2993.name: Church leadership of the DELK (German Evangelical Lutheran Church)
a2993.speech: At a meeting in Windhoek yesterday it dealt with a letter from the Church Foreign Office regarding the dispatch of pastors, after five DELK pastors were recalled by the Council of the EKD.

a2993.speaker: Council of the EKD (Evangelical Church in Germany)
a2993.name: Council of the EKD (Evangelical Church in Germany)
a2993.speech: The Council of the EKD has adopted the five pastors' reasons for their recall as its own. Furthermore, the EKD has made the dispatch of new pastors dependent on various conditions.

a2993.speaker: The five recalled DELK pastors
a2993.name: The five recalled DELK pastors
a2993.speech: The pastors place the blame on their congregations and the Regional Provost.

a2993.speaker: British Labour Party (election manifesto)
a2993.name: British Labour Party (election manifesto)
a2993.speech: The British Labour Party will, if it wins the elections, grant material support to the liberation movements in southern Africa. The party fights all forms of racial discrimination and colonialism. It does not wish for an expansion of acts of violence in southern Africa, since violence is already being committed by the minority regimes. The Labour Party's election manifesto is based on a resolution of last year's party congress.

a2993.speaker: Harold Wilson, British Labour Party leader
a2993.name: Harold Wilson
a2993.title: British Labour Party leader
a2993.speech: Wilson emphasised that it would be best if British aid went through the UN. Wilson also wants to raise the question of EC membership anew and to argue for withdrawal.

a2993.speaker: TASS news agency
a2993.name: TASS news agency
a2993.speech: A report by the TASS agency states that the Supreme Soviet Presidium stripped Solzhenitsyn of his citizenship because of his "systematic activities", which are incompatible with citizenship and damaging to the Soviet Union. He was therefore also deported; his family may follow him later.

a2993.speaker: Alexander Solzhenitsyn, Russian writer
a2993.name: Alexander Solzhenitsyn
a2993.title: Russian writer
