a2993.speech: He asked the German government to protect him from press representatives, and Böll's house is therefore guarded by uniformed police.

a2993.speaker: SWA Meat Trade Control Board (statement)
a2993.name: SWA Meat Trade Control Board (statement)
a2993.speech: The SWA Meat Trade Control Board will not make any allocation of cattle export quotas for the period from April to September, the peak season in cattle marketing; this was decided on Wednesday at a meeting of the Board in Windhoek. Should an oversupply occur, the Board will review its decision and, as required, make an allocation for a month or longer. ; The Meat Trade Control Board has urged the farming community to begin marketing their cattle in good time and to spread exports over as long a period as possible in order to avoid congestion and ensure a smooth marketing process. ; In the case of small stock (sheep and goats), no quotas will be allocated at all, since according to submissions from the farming community there is no need for this; as regards marketing, the statement from the Meat Trade Control Board says, the same applies as for cattle.

a2993.speaker: Quota Allocation Committee
a2993.name: Quota Allocation Committee
a2993.speech: A corresponding recommendation was submitted to the Board by the Quota Allocation Committee.

a2993.speaker: SWA Water-Ski Association
a2993.name: SWA Water-Ski Association
a2993.speech: The SWA Water-Ski Association has submitted an application to the Administration for special permission for a severely restricted practice of the sport on the Von Bach Dam, on the Hardap Dam and in the harbour area of Walvis Bay.

a3129.speaker: Egypt (government)
a3129.name: Egypt (government)
a3129.speech: Has pledged $10m to support agriculture and the fishing sector in South Sudan at the sideline of the UN General Assembly.

a3129.speaker: Chairperson of South Sudanese refugees living in Sudan
a3129.name: Chairperson of South Sudanese refugees living in Sudan
a3129.speech: Says their situation is getting worse due to lack of humanitarian assistance in the camps.

a3129.speaker: South Sudan Council of Churches
a3129.name: South Sudan Council of Churches
a3129.speech: Says it is organizing prayers to be held on Monday, a day after the sixth independence anniversary.

a3129.speaker: Father James Oyet, Secretary General of the South Sudan Council of Churches
a3129.name: Father James Oyet
a3129.title: Secretary General of the South Sudan Council of Churches
a3129.speech: Told Eye Radio that the prayers are for thanking God for the six years of independence and to seek more spiritual guidance to move the country out of the current crisis. “We are going to pray on that day to thank God for the independence of this country, to thank God for the independence of this homeland called South Sudan.” ; “We understand the difficulties we are going through but we want to offer to God, God who knows our hearts, God who knows the hearts of people of South Sudan will listen surely to our prayer. We want to thank him for these six years of independence and we want to ask him to help us out of this crisis.” ; “The day of the pray is Monday 10th July 2017. The prayers will take place at John Garang Mausoleum starting from 10 o’clock and end at mid-day; two hours of medication to God.”

a3129.speaker: Caretaker County Commissioner in Sudan (official order)
a3129.name: Caretaker County Commissioner in Sudan (official order)
a3129.speech: Has issued an order expelling South Sudanese from Al-Dhaen locality in East Darfur State.

a3129.speaker: Governor of Northern Upper Nile
a3129.name: Governor of Northern Upper Nile
a3129.speech: Has said the new states created from the former Upper Nile are not receiving their share of oil revenues due to the current conflict.

a3129.speaker: Ministry of Health and the World Health Organization
a3129.name: Ministry of Health and the World Health Organization
a3129.speech: Have said the outbreak of Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo has been contained.

a3133.speaker: Emmanuel Macron, French President
a3133.name: Emmanuel Macron
a3133.title: French President
a3133.speech: Borrowing the words from the French President that the world is made up of herbivores and carnivores, that if one remains herbivores, then the carnivores will win, and herbivores will be a market for them.

a3204.speaker: Humanitarian sources
a3204.name: Humanitarian sources
a3204.speech: According to humanitarian sources, the Kanyaruchinya site, formerly one of the largest reception centres in the DRC, is today occupied at less than 10% of its capacity, and the Nzulo 1 and Rusayo 2 camps do not exceed 30% occupancy.

a3204.speaker: NGOs
a3204.name: NGOs
a3204.speech: According to NGOs, the consequences are severe: on site, open-air latrines expose the populations to grave health risks.

a3204.speaker: Humanitarian actors
a3204.name: Humanitarian actors
a3204.speech: Are sounding the alarm: cases of cholera have been reported in certain reception sites, notably at Buhimba.

a3204.speaker: Members of the AFC/M23 directorate
a3204.name: Members of the AFC/M23 directorate
a3204.speech: Justify the destruction of these camps by claiming that they sheltered Wazalendo, fighters allied with the DRC's armed forces, and maintain that several of these sites served as refuge for armed groups ; They also say they have asked NGOs wishing to provide humanitarian aid to do so directly in the displaced people's localities of origin.

a3204.speaker: Local sources
a3204.name: Local sources
a3204.speech: Confirm that even after the capture of Minova, in South Kivu province, the AFC/M23 ordered the dismantling of displacement sites, under the direct supervision of its armed elements.

a3470.speaker: United States Embassy in Addis Abeba (statement sent to Fortune)
a3470.name: United States Embassy in Addis Abeba (statement sent to Fortune)
a3470.speech: The United States has been increasingly concerned by the lack of progress toward finalizing an agreement, according to a statement the Embassy sent to Fortune: “The decision to temporarily pause certain assistance for Ethiopia reflects our concern about Ethiopia's unilateral decision to begin filling the Dam before an agreement and safety measures were in place” ; “The pause doesn't apply to humanitarian assistance or to funding that has already been committed for development programmes” ; “An agreement would be transformational and improve the lives of over 250 million people by expanding economic opportunities through transboundary cooperation and regional integration.”

a3470.speaker: United States government
a3470.name: United States government
a3470.speech: Claims that it is involved in the process of supporting a fair and equitable agreement that balances the interests of all three parties.

a3470.speaker: David Shinn, former United States Ambassador to Ethiopia
a3470.name: David Shinn
a3470.title: former United States Ambassador to Ethiopia
a3470.speech: Said the role of the United States in all of this is to pressure Ethiopia to take a position closer to the Egyptians: “The American administration is using high-pressure tactics to try to get Ethiopia to change its position,” he said. “My own view is that it isn't going to work.” ; said it is more a question of power politics from the standpoint of the United States than it is the rightness and wrongness of what any country is doing in terms of releasing water from the reserves.

a3470.speaker: Fitsum Arega, Ethiopian Ambassador to the United States (tweets)
a3470.name: Fitsum Arega
a3470.title: Ethiopian Ambassador to the United States (tweets)
a3470.speech: Tweeted last week that the Embassy requested a clarification from the United States government and they were told that the aid cut is a “temporary pause” ; “It's our Dam!” tweeted Fitsum, “We'll finish it together! With our effort, Ethiopia will shine.”

a3470.speaker: Dina Mufti, spokesperson at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (non-response)
a3470.name: Dina Mufti
a3470.title: spokesperson at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (non-response)
a3470.speech: Did not respond to a phone call and text message from Fortune before the paper was sent to print.

a3572.speaker: Roukya Ali Djama, project director (UNFD)
a3572.name: Roukya Ali Djama
a3572.title: project director (UNFD)
a3572.speech: Placed the emphasis on the UNFD's activities, adding that “the UNFD is currently working on five-year strategic planning for the period 2020-2024; we work in various fields, notably in the field of education and health, and it turned out to be necessary to be able to exchange and discuss with the country's NGOs the actions the UNFD undertakes in the various fields, and it was also a matter of speaking about our challenges and our strengths and weaknesses, but also our opportunities at the level of the UNFD. This two-day workshop on strategic planning will make it possible to improve the visibility of the UNFD's actions, but also to be able to facilitate advocacy and fundraising.”

a3572.speaker: Larry Andre, United States Ambassador to Djibouti
a3572.name: Larry Andre
a3572.title: United States Ambassador to Djibouti
a3572.speech: Said he was delighted to come to the UNFD's headquarters, and congratulated the UNFD's leaders for the work they accomplish every day in favour of the living conditions of the Djiboutian population.

a3590.speaker: Duma Boko, President of Botswana
a3590.name: Duma Boko
a3590.title: President of Botswana
a3590.speech: told industry leaders at the JCK Las Vegas Trade Show of Botswana's evolving diamond industry and the country's ambitions to become a global hub for ethical luxury and innovation: "Botswana is open for investment and ready to partner," underscoring a new strategy aimed at attracting global players to sectors such as luxury goods, tourism, green energy, and technology.

a3590.speaker: Duma Boko, President of Botswana
a3590.name: Duma Boko
a3590.title: President of Botswana
a3590.speech: highlighted the recently concluded agreement with De Beers as a cornerstone of this new direction: "This agreement includes significant investments in local beneficiation, skills development, and infrastructure" ; referenced De Beers' decision to shut down its Lightbox synthetic diamond business, interpreting it as a "shared commitment to natural diamonds."

a3590.speaker: Duma Boko, President of Botswana
a3590.name: Duma Boko
a3590.title: President of Botswana
a3590.speech: stated that Botswana is streamlining its investment framework to eliminate unnecessary bureaucracy, noting the country's favourable credit rating - BBB+ long-term and A-2 short-term by Standard & Poor's - while emphasising the need for more than just strong financial indicators: "We are acting with urgency to make Botswana an easier, faster and more transparent place to do business."

a3590.speaker: Duma Boko, President of Botswana
a3590.name: Duma Boko
a3590.title: President of Botswana
a3590.speech: highlighted Botswana's environmental commitments, pointing to a new agreement between Debswana and Botswana Power Corporation to supply renewable energy for mining operations: "This partnership enables Debswana to power its operations with clean electricity," adding that Botswana aims to become carbon neutral by 2030.

a3590.speaker: Duma Boko, President of Botswana
a3590.name: Duma Boko
a3590.title: President of Botswana
a3590.speech: stressed investment in marketing, traceability and consumer education: "Confidence is the cornerstone of luxury, and we will protect that confidence with everything we have."

a3590.speaker: Duma Boko, President of Botswana
a3590.name: Duma Boko
a3590.title: President of Botswana
a3590.speech: spoke of ambitions to build Botswana into a destination for Meetings, Incentives, Conferences, and Events (MICE), and to develop new economic sectors that reduce reliance on raw exports: "Botswana is ready to be known not just for exporting diamonds but also for exporting inspiration."

a3612.speaker: Ministry of Finance of Mozambique (official public debt bulletin, first quarter of 2025)
a3612.name: Ministry of Finance of Mozambique (official public debt bulletin
a3612.title: first quarter of 2025)
a3612.speech: The official bulletin leaves no room for deliberate illusions: the total stock of Government debt, on behalf of the State, exceeds 1 trillion meticais, with quarterly growth of 2.7% driven above all by domestic debt, fed by successive issues of treasury bills and Central Bank credit.

a3612.speaker: Proposed Economic and Social Plan and State Budget (PESOE) 2025 (government document)
a3612.name: Proposed Economic and Social Plan and State Budget (PESOE) 2025 (government document)
a3612.speech: Foresees budget reductions in several strategic sectors: Education, a 3.7% cut against the 2024 budget; Health, a 2.2% reduction on the previous year; Infrastructure (roads, housing, sanitation), a 14.5% cut; Water supply and water resources, an 18.3% cut; and Energy, a significant 21.9% cut.

a3612.speaker: International Growth Centre (IGC) study
a3612.name: International Growth Centre (IGC) study
a3612.speech: According to data from an IGC study — an applied research institution created by the University of Oxford in partnership with the London School of Economics (LSE) — Mozal is among the cleanest aluminium operations in the world ; According to the IGC analysis, introducing a carbon price in line with the European CBAM (around USD 96 per tonne of CO₂) would not negatively affect Mozal’s competitiveness, because its carbon intensity is low and the carbon cost would in any case be unavoidable at European borders.

a3630.speaker: Protesters in Kismayo
a3630.name: Protesters in Kismayo
a3630.speech: Expressed strong opposition to the Somali government's flight embargo imposed on Jubaland; denounced President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud's policies, with many demanding his resignation, accusing his administration of deepening national divisions rather than fostering unity; carried placards that sharply criticized both the president and his government.

a3630.speaker: Jubaland authorities (declaration)
a3630.name: Jubaland authorities (declaration)
a3630.speech: Stated their intent to independently engage with the international community, and announced that foreign aid designated for the region will no longer be channeled through the federal government.

a3750.speaker: Donald Trump, President of the United States
a3750.name: Donald Trump
a3750.title: President of the United States
a3750.speech: On Monday 3 March ordered a “pause” in United States military aid to Ukraine, halting not only new aid to come but also aid already approved by the former Biden administration and not yet delivered.

a3750.speaker: Donald Trump, President of the United States
a3750.name: Donald Trump
a3750.title: President of the United States
a3750.speech: Estimated the aid provided to Ukraine at 350 billion dollars.

a3750.speaker: Numerous American politicians
a3750.name: Numerous American politicians
a3750.speech: Described the Ukrainian president's behaviour as shameful and advocated the cessation of all relations with him.

a3750.speaker: Michael Johnson, Speaker of the House of Representatives, and Mike Waltz, National Security Adviser
a3750.name: Michael Johnson
a3750.title: Speaker of the House of Representatives, and Mike Waltz, National Security Adviser
a3750.speech: Trump's biggest supporters called on Zelensky to resign; this was notably declared by the Speaker of the House of Representatives, Michael Johnson, as well as by the National Security Adviser, Mike Waltz.

a3750.speaker: Military analysts
a3750.name: Military analysts
a3750.speech: According to the forecasts of military analysts, without American financial aid and the supply of weapons, Ukraine can still hold out for six months.

a3750.speaker: Wall Street Journal
a3750.name: Wall Street Journal
a3750.speech: Notes, rightly, that munitions for Patriot air-defence systems are manufactured only in the United States and that with the cessation of deliveries the Ukrainian armed forces will quickly face a shortage of missiles and will have to choose which sites to protect and which to leave undefended.

a3750.speaker: BBC
a3750.name: BBC
a3750.speech: Writes that there is nothing to replace these missiles (GMLRS/ATACMS), neither quantitatively nor qualitatively.

a3750.speaker: CNN
a3750.name: CNN
a3750.speech: Indicates that “the United States and Europe have the capacity to produce only about 1.2 million munitions per year”.

a3750.speaker: Mikola Malomuz, army general and former head of Ukraine's foreign intelligence service
a3750.name: Mikola Malomuz
a3750.title: army general and former head of Ukraine's foreign intelligence service
a3750.speech: Told the Ukrainian channel “Channel 24” what consequences the cessation of intelligence exchange between Washington and Kyiv could entail; according to him, halting the transfer of data from space and technical intelligence and from the network of intelligence agents will be an immense loss for Ukraine, because American intelligence is far more advantageous than that of even the large European countries.

a3750.speaker: Oleg Nesterenko, President of the CCIE, specialist in Russia, the CIS and sub-Saharan Africa, former MBA director and former professor at the masters programmes of the Paris Grandes Ecoles de Commerce (author of the opinion piece)
a3750.name: Oleg Nesterenko
a3750.title: President of the CCIE, specialist in Russia, the CIS and sub-Saharan Africa, former MBA director and former professor at the masters programmes of the Paris Grandes Ecoles de Commerce (author of the opinion piece)
a3750.speech: Argues that the Ukrainian leader Volodymyr Zelensky bears personal responsibility for the incident and had no moral right to display his temper before the country on which Ukraine vitally depends; that the cessation of American military aid is quite simply fatal for the Ukrainian army's capacity to fight; and that, with the rejection of the peace agreement and the rupture of relations with the United States, Ukrainian society is dominated by panic over the inevitability of the coming military defeat, with the population condemned to live on the economic, social and cultural ruins of the country.

a3859.speaker: Shamika N. Sirimanne, head of the CSTD Secretariat
a3859.name: Shamika N. Sirimanne
a3859.title: head of the CSTD Secretariat
a3859.speech: “Science, technology and innovation provide a shining light to help us navigate and recover from the COVID-19 pandemic.” ; “We'll use this meeting to discuss how we can foster international collaboration in science and technology, not only to tackle and recover from the virus, but also to address other pressing sustainable development concerns, which range from climate change to inequality.” ; said STI-related activities should be incorporated in recovery packages. Not only can this spur economic activity, but it can also enhance the resilience of countries to cope with future crises.

a3859.speaker: UN Commission on Science and Technology for Development (CSTD)
a3859.name: UN Commission on Science and Technology for Development (CSTD)
a3859.speech: has consistently emphasized that technological change is essential to achieving all the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

a3940.speaker: Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State
a3940.name: Marco Rubio
a3940.title: US Secretary of State
a3940.speech: Announced the waiver for PEPFAR to provide HIV medications to poor nations: “All implementing U.S. government agencies, partners, and NGOs, for the purposes of carrying out...”

a3946.speaker: Filipe Nyusi, Mozambican President
a3946.name: Filipe Nyusi
a3946.title: Mozambican President
a3946.speech: Declared on Thursday that no elephants have been poached since 2018 in the Niassa Special Reserve, the largest conservation area in the country: “The investments and the legal reforms we have been undertaking in the conservation areas have brought a new dynamic and important gains for the Reserve” ; said poaching had been reduced through the recruitment of more rangers, who now used boats and aircraft as well as conventional means of land transport.

a3946.speaker: Filipe Nyusi, Mozambican President
a3946.name: Filipe Nyusi
a3946.title: Mozambican President
a3946.speech: Thanked the defence and security forces for their cooperation with the Niassa rangers, and added that the increase in the number of partners and “the healthy coexistence between the various operators, alongside the government and the communities” had also contributed to a healthy environment for the development of the Reserve.

a3946.speaker: Filipe Nyusi, Mozambican President
a3946.name: Filipe Nyusi
a3946.title: Mozambican President
a3946.speech: “The Mozambican state will continue to do its part by investing in a programme of monitoring, through placing collars and satellite tracking of the iconic animals of the Reserve… ensuring their continued protection and the integrity of their habitats” ; “This is a re-affirmation of our commitment to the conservation of biodiversity, and of emblematic species in particular… This is an activity we promise to follow and to honour, in defence of our entire planet, our collective home.”

a3946.speaker: Helen Pataki, USAID director in Mozambique
a3946.name: Helen Pataki
a3946.title: USAID director in Mozambique
a3946.speech: Said that American support had played a determinant role in the fight against poaching: “Support from the US Government’s Aerial Vigilance Programme has allowed monitoring, and also the deployment of patrols… This has led to a reduction in the cases of illegal mining and logging in the reserve, as well as cutting to zero the poaching of elephants since 2018.”

a3946.speaker: Helen Pataki, USAID director in Mozambique
a3946.name: Helen Pataki
a3946.title: USAID director in Mozambique
a3946.speech: Stressed that the preservation of biodiversity is a necessity in a world facing the threats of climate change and environmental degradation.

a4053.speaker: Save The Children (report)
a4053.name: Save The Children (report)
a4053.speech: recent report that four African countries, including Nigeria, Kenya, Somalia and South Sudan, are expected to run out of ready-to-use emergency food over the next three months due to aid cuts if gaps are not plugged, putting severely malnourished children at risk of dying.

a4053.speaker: United Nations Children's Fund (UNICEF) report of 2024
a4053.name: United Nations Children's Fund (UNICEF) report of 2024
a4053.speech: said that "Around 11 million children, or one in every three children under five years of age in Nigeria, are experiencing severe child food poverty, making them up to 50 percent more likely to experience wasting, a life-threatening form of malnutrition."

a4053.speaker: Professor Sharkdam Wapmuk, Department of Defence and Security Studies, Nigerian Defence Academy (NDA), Kaduna and former Senior Research Fellow, Nigerian Institute of International Affairs (NIIA)
a4053.name: Professor Sharkdam Wapmuk
a4053.title: Department of Defence and Security Studies, Nigerian Defence Academy (NDA), Kaduna and former Senior Research Fellow, Nigerian Institute of International Affairs (NIIA)
a4053.speech: alerted the Nigerian government that the slash in assistance given to the country by the United States government and other Western powers risks fuelling further insecurity, as hunger and malnutrition can trigger social unrest, displacement, and recruitment into violent groups, particularly in the North-East and North-West.

a4053.speaker: Professor Sharkdam Wapmuk, international relations expert
a4053.name: Professor Sharkdam Wapmuk
a4053.title: international relations expert
a4053.speech: said that this "development will have grave implications for Nigeria." ; warned that "Any disruption in external humanitarian aid will increase child mortality rates, worsen health crises, and deepen poverty in vulnerable regions." ; said the development "In the long term, undermines Nigeria's human capital development and weakens the country's capacity to achieve sustainable growth."

a4053.speaker: Professor Sharkdam Wapmuk, international relations expert
a4053.name: Professor Sharkdam Wapmuk
a4053.title: international relations expert
a4053.speech: said that "Nigeria must prioritise domestic interventions that reduce dependence on external aid", including "strengthening food security through investment in local agriculture, irrigation, and food storage systems, especially in conflict-prone areas" and "Expanding community-based nutrition programmes, scaling up access to ready-to-use therapeutic food (RUTF), and supporting local production of nutrition supplements are critical." ; suggested that the "The Nigerian government must also continue to curtail the activities of middlemen who buy and hoard food to sell at higher prices, and ensure effective distribution mechanisms. Food security is not only about food production, but also about access, affordability, and nutritional value." ; called for "stronger partnerships between the government, the private sector, and humanitarian organizations to ensure that aid shortfalls are bridged through domestic innovation and sustainable funding."

a4053.speaker: Professor Sharkdam Wapmuk, international relations expert
a4053.name: Professor Sharkdam Wapmuk
a4053.title: international relations expert
a4053.speech: suggested: "The Nigerian government can discourage dependence on foreign aid by deliberately investing in local food production and nutrition industries, rather than depending on imported or donor-driven supplies." ; said that "This requires policies that support farmers with credit, technology, and infrastructure, while also reducing insecurity in food-producing regions." ; added that "Nigeria must strengthen fiscal discipline, reduce corruption in the food and health sectors, and channel oil revenues into social safety nets." ; stressed that "Building resilience through home-grown solutions will not only save lives but also project Nigeria as a country capable of addressing its humanitarian and developmental challenges without undue dependence on foreign actors."

a4322.speaker: Participants in the demonstration in Niamey (representatives of various parties and trade union associations)
a4322.name: Participants in the demonstration in Niamey (representatives of various parties and trade union associations)
a4322.speech: Took to the streets to express support for the country’s ruling National Council for the Defense of the Fatherland and condemn imperialism and neocolonialism; emphasised the important role of youth in confronting external challenges and uniting the nation, critically assessed the position of ECOWAS in relation to Niger, and during their speeches expressed gratitude to the new authorities for opposing neocolonialism and removing the country from the sphere of influence of France and the United States.

a4322.speaker: Military personnel of the presidential Guard, Niger
a4322.name: Military personnel of the presidential Guard
a4322.title: Niger
a4322.speech: On July 26, 2023, announced the removal of President Mohamed Bazoum.

a4322.speaker: Leaders of most Western countries and ECOWAS
a4322.name: Leaders of most Western countries and ECOWAS

a4322.speaker: Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS)
a4322.name: Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS)
a4322.speech: Said in December that it would provide Niger, Mali and Burkina Faso with a period from January 29 to July 29, 2025, to review their decision to withdraw from the bloc.

a4367.speaker: Yiorgos Christopoulos, General Confederation of Workers (GSEE)
a4367.name: Yiorgos Christopoulos
a4367.title: General Confederation of Workers (GSEE)
a4367.speech: Told Al Jazeera: “Our confederation’s wage demand is to bring back collective wage bargaining. Before 2012, half of Greek workers had collective wage agreements. But there was also a national wage agreement signed by employers and unions which meant more than 90 percent of workers enjoyed maternity leave.” ; “Now the government has put individual contracts at the heart of its policy. But individuals are powerless to bargain [with] their employers.”

a4367.speaker: General Confederation of Workers (GSEE) (statement)
a4367.name: General Confederation of Workers (GSEE) (statement)
a4367.speech: “Prices have gone so high that we’re buying fewer goods by 10 percent compared to 2019. We’re striking for the obvious. Pay rises and collective labour contracts now!”

a4367.speaker: Greek labour unions
a4367.name: Greek labour unions
a4367.speech: Say that many households still struggle to make ends meet amid rising food, power and housing costs, despite the conservative government increasing the monthly minimum wage by a cumulative 35 percent to 880 euros ($970).

a4411.speaker: China’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs (@MFA_China post)
a4411.name: China’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs (@MFA_China post)
a4411.speech: "In response to the U.S.’s illegal unilateral sanctions against Chinese officials in Hong Kong, China decided to impose sanctions on the U.S. Congress members, government officials and heads of NGOs who acted egregiously on #HongKong-related issues."

a4411.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a4411.name: Donald Trump
a4411.title: US President
a4411.speech: Has said China needs to make the first move in any negotiation ; "The ball is in China's court. China needs to make a deal with us. We don't have to make a deal with them," a day after accusing Beijing of reneging on a major Boeing deal.

a4411.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a4411.name: Donald Trump
a4411.title: US President
a4411.speech: Authorised an investigation into “national security risks posed by the U.S.' reliance on imported, processed critical minerals and derived products,” which includes cobalt, lithium, nickel, and rare-earth metals used in the manufacture of smartphones, batteries for electric vehicles, and military equipment.

a4411.speaker: Bloomberg News (citing people familiar with the matter)
a4411.name: Bloomberg News (citing people familiar with the matter)
a4411.speech: Reported on Tuesday that China has ordered its airlines not to take any further deliveries of Boeing jets, and that Beijing has also instructed Chinese carriers to halt purchases of aircraft-related equipment and parts from U.S. companies.

a4411.speaker: Sources familiar with the matter (anonymous), told Bloomberg News
a4411.name: Sources familiar with the matter (anonymous)
a4411.title: told Bloomberg News
a4411.speech: Said the Chinese government is reportedly considering ways to assist airlines leasing Boeing jets who are facing increased costs.

a4411.speaker: Chinese officials (statement published on the customs department website)
a4411.name: Chinese officials (statement published on the customs department website)
a4411.speech: Accused the United States of violating international trade norms.

a4411.speaker: China
a4411.name: China
a4411.speech: Has vowed to "fight till its end" in what it called efforts to tackle the United States' monopoly on trade.

a4499.speaker: U.N. AIDS agency (UNAIDS)
a4499.name: U.N. AIDS agency (UNAIDS)
a4499.speech: "In the next five years, we could have 6.3 million AIDS-related deaths," the U.N. AIDS agency told The Associated Press.

a4499.speaker: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
a4499.name: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
a4499.speech: "Without HIV treatment, people with AIDS typically survive about three years," the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention says.

a4499.speaker: National Institutes of Health (NIH)
a4499.name: National Institutes of Health (NIH)
a4499.speech: Says opportunistic diseases include fungal infections, pneumonia, salmonella and tuberculosis.

a4499.speaker: Health experts
a4499.name: Health experts
a4499.speech: Say that restoring the effects caused by the Trump administration's foreign aid freeze during a 90-day review period, and understanding what's allowed under the waiver for PEPFAR, will take time that many people don't have; health experts, patients and others fear the days of AIDS wards could return if the Trump administration doesn't reverse course or no other global power steps into the void, and fast.

a4499.speaker: Winnie Byanyima, head of the U.N. AIDS agency
a4499.name: Winnie Byanyima
a4499.title: head of the U.N. AIDS agency
a4499.speech: Told the AP that more resistant strains of the disease could emerge.

a4508.speaker: U.S. Mission Nigeria (announcement)
a4508.name: U.S. Mission Nigeria (announcement)
a4508.speech: "The U.S. Mission is pleased to announce the arrival of its new Consul General, Rick Swart, who arrived in Lagos on July 16."

a4508.speaker: Rick Swart, U.S. Consul General in Lagos
a4508.name: Rick Swart
a4508.title: U.S. Consul General in Lagos
a4508.speech: "I am honored to serve in Nigeria," Consul General Swart said. "I am excited about the opportunity to travel across the region, meet the people, experience the culture, while advancing the shared goals of making our two countries safer, stronger, and more prosperous." ; "I look forward to working closely with Ambassador Mills and the team at the U.S. Embassy in Abuja, to further advance the shared objectives between Nigeria and the United States."

a4508.speaker: Rick Swart, U.S. Consul General in Lagos
a4508.name: Rick Swart
a4508.title: U.S. Consul General in Lagos
a4508.speech: "I thank JoEllen for her remarkable leadership and for the outstanding work she has done to promote our close partnership with the Nigerian people in the region," Consul General Swart added.

a4524.speaker: Notícias ao Minuto (website)
a4524.name: Notícias ao Minuto (website)
a4524.speech: Reported that, under the slogans "UN staff are not a commodity" and "We defend humanity", the demonstration was attended by Public Services International (PSI), the Federation of International Civil Servants' Associations (FICSA) and the Coordinating Committee for International Staff Unions and Associations of the United Nations System (CCISUA).

a4524.speaker: Daniel Bertossa, general secretary of Public Services International (PSI)
a4524.name: Daniel Bertossa
a4524.title: general secretary of Public Services International (PSI)
a4524.speech: "We are in a very difficult and unfortunate situation, in which it is not only the world's governments that are under attack, but also the UN and its agencies," said at the protest demonstration.

a4524.speaker: EFE (news agency)
a4524.name: EFE (news agency)
a4524.speech: According to the agency, the situation is being aggravated by the withdrawal of a large part of the aid of its main contributor, the government of the United States.

a4524.speaker: Severine Deboos, president of the union of workers of the International Labour Organization (ILO)
a4524.name: Severine Deboos
a4524.title: president of the union of workers of the International Labour Organization (ILO)
a4524.speech: "We are not a commodity, but human beings who have the right to good working conditions and to respect for our dignity."

a4524.speaker: Organisers of the demonstration
a4524.name: Organisers of the demonstration
a4524.speech: According to them, following the drastic cut in US aid, the UN Refugee Agency (UNHCR) and the World Food Programme (WFP) have reduced staff worldwide by around 30%, while the ILO has cut 10% of its jobs.

a4524.speaker: Nathalie Meynet and Cristina Pierini, leaders of CCISUA and FICSA
a4524.name: Nathalie Meynet and Cristina Pierini
a4524.title: leaders of CCISUA and FICSA
a4524.speech: "These are not just statistics; behind them are thousands of people who deliver humanitarian aid, secure access to drinking water, food and health care, protect refugees and displaced people, keep children in school, prevent forced labour and defend human rights."

a4805.speaker: Abdoulaye Seydou, Minister of Trade and Industry of Niger
a4805.name: Abdoulaye Seydou
a4805.title: Minister of Trade and Industry of Niger
a4805.speech: Reminded his interlocutors that the State of Niger, in its determination to guarantee food sovereignty and strengthen food security, had taken the measure banning the export of paddy rice, milled rice, millet, sorghum, cowpeas and maize so that the population could genuinely have access to widely consumed products. He made it clear that in its implementation “some tried to contravene that order and that impacted them negatively,” stressing that it is in order not to relive the same difficulties as last year that they deemed it useful to organise this meeting. “Better to prevent than to cure.”

a4805.speaker: Abdoulaye Seydou, Minister of Trade and Industry of Niger
a4805.name: Abdoulaye Seydou
a4805.title: Minister of Trade and Industry of Niger
a4805.speech: Expressed satisfaction that today, thanks to this measure and many other factors, the prices of widely consumed products are affordable. “When I take as an example today, millet has seen a fall of around 34% compared with last year, sorghum 43%, maize 40% and imported rice 20%.” He specifies that the measure does not imply a ban on the marketing of these products, insofar as, although prices are at a very low level in the agricultural parts of the country, there is a certain part of the country where prices are quite high.

a4805.speaker: Abdoulaye Seydou, Minister of Trade and Industry of Niger
a4805.name: Abdoulaye Seydou
a4805.title: Minister of Trade and Industry of Niger
a4805.speech: Said the order enshrined an exceptional measure for the AES countries, notably Mali and Burkina, or perhaps friendly countries: “despite this exception, before traders can try to export those products to those countries, the normal procedure will have to be genuinely respected.”

a4805.speaker: Abdoulaye Seydou, Minister of Trade and Industry of Niger
a4805.name: Abdoulaye Seydou
a4805.title: Minister of Trade and Industry of Niger
a4805.speech: Warned “that all offenders will expose themselves to the sanctions laid down by the order. It is first of all the seizure of those products and their transfer to the solidarity fund in accordance with the second order that was issued. Beyond the products or the cereals, it is also the vehicles used to transport those products.” He asks the participants to sensitise their members that this order is still in force until it is decided otherwise.

a4805.speaker: Abdoulaye Seydou, Minister of Trade and Industry of Niger
a4805.name: Abdoulaye Seydou
a4805.title: Minister of Trade and Industry of Niger
a4805.speech: While reassuring that they have no will or intention to kill the cereals trade, made it known that at the time the decision was taken, “there were people who were put in place to buy up the products and create a shortage of widely consumed food products in our country so that it could lead to the destabilisation of our country.”

a4805.speaker: Members of the National Union of Importers and Exporters of Cereals (traders)
a4805.name: Members of the National Union of Importers and Exporters of Cereals (traders)
a4805.speech: Raised certain concerns, on which the Minister gave further clarification, and welcomed this initiative by the Minister.

a4832.speaker: R-JMEC (Reconstituted Joint Monitoring and Evaluation Commission)
a4832.name: R-JMEC (Reconstituted Joint Monitoring and Evaluation Commission)
a4832.speech: has called on South Sudan peace parties to cease hostilities and the incumbent transitional government to immediately release the SPLM/A-IO leaders and military officials currently in detention, unless credible evidence warrants legal proceedings; recommends to all peace parties and relevant stakeholders to cease all forms of hostility and restore adherence to the Permanent Ceasefire and Transitional Security Arrangements, and allow CTSAMVM the opportunity to investigate, verify and report findings on alleged violations.

a4832.speaker: Amb. Maj. Gen. (rtd) George Aggrey Owinow, R-JMEC Interim Chairperson
a4832.name: Amb. Maj. Gen. (rtd) George Aggrey Owinow
a4832.title: R-JMEC Interim Chairperson
a4832.speech: said in a 24-page report on the status of the peace accord that the peace implementation ground to a halt in the first quarter of the year, as the parties engaged in repeated violations and the political and security environment worsened; noted that in scenes not seen since the signing of the R-ARCSS over six years ago, armed conflict and violence erupted across the country, and several high-ranking opposition members were detained and imprisoned.

a4832.speaker: Amb. Maj. Gen. (rtd) George Aggrey Owinow, R-JMEC Interim Chairperson
a4832.name: Amb. Maj. Gen. (rtd) George Aggrey Owinow
a4832.title: R-JMEC Interim Chairperson
a4832.speech: citing the Communique of the 43rd Extraordinary Summit of IGAD Heads of State and Government, called for the immediate release of the SPLM/A-IO leaders and military officials currently in detention, unless credible evidence warrants legal proceedings conducted transparently and in accordance with due process.

a4832.speaker: Amb. Maj. Gen. (rtd) George Aggrey Owinow, R-JMEC Interim Chairperson
a4832.name: Amb. Maj. Gen. (rtd) George Aggrey Owinow
a4832.title: R-JMEC Interim Chairperson
a4832.speech: encouraged peace parties to reactivate and re-energize the functionality of all the Agreement implementation institutions and mechanisms, especially the Transitional Security Mechanisms, rebuild trust and confidence in the peace process and prioritize completion of the critical pending tasks; encouraged diplomatic and political support from the regional guarantors and international partners that serve to deescalate tensions and support dialogue; called for the prioritization of the unification of all forces, deployment of the Necessary Unified Forces (NUF), implementation of comprehensive DDR, and expedited implementation of the Judicial Reform Committee (JRC) report.

a4832.speaker: Amb. Maj. Gen. (rtd) George Aggrey Owinow, R-JMEC Interim Chairperson
a4832.name: Amb. Maj. Gen. (rtd) George Aggrey Owinow
a4832.title: R-JMEC Interim Chairperson
a4832.speech: said security violations reportedly committed by both the SSPDF and the SPLA-IO now threaten the peace and stability of South Sudan; said in some parts of the country civilians including women and children have borne the brunt of the fallout and have suffered serious human rights and humanitarian law violations including death, injury and displacement; noted: "There has been no progress regarding the unification and deployment of forces, which under the R-ARCSS was intended to bring the former warring parties together under one unified command. Phase I deployment has not been completed, and Phase II training has not yet started."

a4832.speaker: R-JMEC report on the status of the peace accord (24-page document)
a4832.name: R-JMEC report on the status of the peace accord (24-page document)
a4832.speech: added that ministerial positions at the state and national levels were reshuffled, and portfolios within some Agreement institutions and mechanisms were abandoned: "Some replacements involved a party to the R-ARCSS replacing its own appointees, whereas in others, the replacements were drawn from different parties. It should be noted that the Agreement is premised on the principles of collegiality, consultation and consensus."

a4832.speaker: R-JMEC report on the status of the peace accord (24-page document)
a4832.name: R-JMEC report on the status of the peace accord (24-page document)
a4832.speech: said South Sudan continued to face a severe humanitarian crisis, further escalated by widespread violence, intercommunal clashes, land disputes, insecurity, natural disasters, cholera outbreak and cross-border movements: "The widespread violence led to increased numbers of Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs) requiring urgent humanitarian assistance."

a4832.speaker: R-JMEC report on the status of the peace accord (24-page document)
a4832.name: R-JMEC report on the status of the peace accord (24-page document)
a4832.speech: said on Economic and Financial Management that the Public Financial Management Oversight Committee identified several priorities in their mid-term strategy: "Of these, nine are contained in the provisions of the R-ARCSS and the assessment focuses on the implementation of these provisions. Progress has also been made with the implementation of the Treasury Single Account (TSA)"; added that very little progress was registered in the implementation of tasks associated with Transitional Justice, Accountability, Reconciliation and Healing.

a4832.speaker: R-JMEC report on the status of the peace accord (24-page document)
a4832.name: R-JMEC report on the status of the peace accord (24-page document)
a4832.speech: added that there is no doubt that the R-ARCSS remains the most viable framework to steer South Sudan towards the path of stability and prosperity, "However, the current political and security situation is fragile and highly volatile, posing a serious threat to the survivability of the R-ARCSS"; "The ongoing political conflicts are also eroding opportunities the extension provided to enhance the integration of gender equality perspectives into the peace process and better prepare women for meaningful participation in the transitional justice, constitution-making and political processes ahead of the anticipated elections in December 2026."

a4832.speaker: Communique of the 43rd Extraordinary Summit of IGAD Heads of State and Government
a4832.name: Communique of the 43rd Extraordinary Summit of IGAD Heads of State and Government
a4832.speech: cited as calling for the immediate release of the SPLM/A-IO leaders and military officials currently in detention.

a4832.speaker: Nicholas Haysom, Special Representative of the UN Secretary-General and Head of UNMISS
a4832.name: Nicholas Haysom
a4832.title: Special Representative of the UN Secretary-General and Head of UNMISS
a4832.speech: warned that the country was on the brink of another civil war and urged all parties in South Sudan to pull back from the brink and commit to peace before the country plunges into another devastating conflict: "A conflict would erase all the hard-won gains made since the 2018 peace deal was signed. It would devastate not only South Sudan but the entire region, which simply cannot afford another war."

a4832.speaker: Jim Risch, Chairman of the U.S. Senate Foreign Relations Committee
a4832.name: Jim Risch
a4832.title: Chairman of the U.S. Senate Foreign Relations Committee
a4832.speech: said South Sudan was close to renewed war and President Salva Kiir and First Vice President Riek Machar bear direct responsibility for the conflict.

a4866.speaker: Andrew 'Andy' Keatlholetswe, former eBotswana television channel employee
a4866.name: Andrew 'Andy' Keatlholetswe
a4866.title: former eBotswana television channel employee
a4866.speech: Says he regrets the day he ever met former president Ian Khama as his life has now turned miserable because of their soured relations; says he met Khama when he was still vice president to Festus Mogae: "I was working and we would interview him, that is how he got to know me. He was very friendly and whenever he saw me, he would make sure he greets me or even shakes my hand" ; "I visited him there and we often talked. He would always call to check up on me. I attended Botswana Democratic Party (BDP) events where we would meet and talk. But all changed when people began passing remarks that I might be gay and even implying that I was having sexual relations with the president. The remarks did not seat well with me, so one day I wrote on Facebook that I hate gays... Then a few days later when attending the Botswana Democratic Party (BDP) conference, Khama saw me but did not smile at me or call me over as he usually did. On the day, he went past me like he did not know me" ; "It is weird because this is the same man who at one point even asked me who I think would be better placed to be his Vice President" ; "People knew that they could not speak ill about him around me. We clicked and he even asked me to join the Directorate of Intelligence Services (DIS) but I refused," saying he refused because the DIS was being associated with all things evil.

a4866.speaker: Andrew 'Andy' Keatlholetswe, former eBotswana television channel employee
a4866.name: Andrew 'Andy' Keatlholetswe
a4866.title: former eBotswana television channel employee
a4866.speech: Says his movements, what he does and says are being monitored, and suspects allies of the former president who are still working in the country's intelligence agency: "There are people who are following me around and have been doing so for some time. When I share this, people think am crazy. I have even been taken to Sbrana Psychiatric Hospital before because they thought I am unwell. At some point I had to lie saying I do not think people are still following me, just so that I am not treated as a mental health patient anymore" ; "I really do not know what he wants from me. I am often asked why I say it's him who is behind this thing of people following me, but I just know it's him. Strange things happen to me, I cannot even date anyone because they mess up my relationships. I once dated an American girl, she dumped me after she was sent pictures of me with girls I did not know..." ; "I know it's him. I just want him to leave me alone. I was even supposed to leave for the United States of America but I am facing inexplicable obstacles that seem to be a part of making my life miserable. I therefore regret the day I met that man. All I want is for his people to leave me alone."

a4866.speaker: Andrew 'Andy' Keatlholetswe, former eBotswana television channel employee
a4866.name: Andrew 'Andy' Keatlholetswe
a4866.title: former eBotswana television channel employee
a4866.speech: Responding to Khama's denial, was quick to provide pictures of himself with Khama saying there is no how he can claim not to know him, saying the two had interacted a lot: "I got included into the communications team because of his instructions, people will be shocked to hear him deny any knowledge of me."

a4866.speaker: Andrew 'Andy' Keatlholetswe, former eBotswana television channel employee
a4866.name: Andrew 'Andy' Keatlholetswe
a4866.title: former eBotswana television channel employee
a4866.speech: "My family has been trying to stop me from talking to the media about this issue, they are worried and I understand but I have long wanted this story to be heard. They do not want to believe me when I say am being followed, my life is a living hell. I at one point resorted to taking some substances after being told they would keep me awake at night. I am not proud of it but I wanted to protect my life" ; "I am perfectly fine, since that time, I have never been to Sbrana again. I do not hate the former president. I actually still care very much about him. Even if he was in danger, I would help him. I just want him to stop making my life a living hell."

a4866.speaker: Ian Khama, former President of Botswana
a4866.name: Ian Khama
a4866.title: former President of Botswana
a4866.speech: When contacted about the matter, denied any knowledge of Andy: "I do not know him at all," Khama said in his response.

a4866.speaker: A man who identified himself as brother to Andy
a4866.name: A man who identified himself as brother to Andy
a4866.speech: Said they are concerned about him; speaking to The Midweek Sun, hinted that Andy might be targeting Khama because he and the former president were once very close, could not dwell on details of the relationship although he promised that the family would speak to this publication in detail about their concerns, and hinted at the feeling by some in the family that he could be unwell mentally.

a4866.speaker: Motsholetsi Keatlholetswe, a man who identified himself as uncle to the two brothers
a4866.name: Motsholetsi Keatlholetswe
a4866.title: a man who identified himself as uncle to the two brothers
a4866.speech: Said the family was no longer interested in commenting on the issue.

a4866.speaker: Attending doctor, Sbrana Psychiatric Hospital (medical records provided by Andy)
a4866.name: Attending doctor
a4866.title: Sbrana Psychiatric Hospital (medical records provided by Andy)
a4866.speech: Records show he was admitted to Sbrana on 29 September 2019 and discharged on 5 October, with the doctor attending to him stating, "The patient was observed in the ward and did not show any abnormal behavior."

a4942.speaker: Heads of State and Government of the East African Community (EAC) and the Southern African Development Community (SADC) (Dar es Salaam summit)
a4942.name: Heads of State and Government of the East African Community (EAC) and the Southern African Development Community (SADC) (Dar es Salaam summit)
a4942.speech: demanded an immediate ceasefire and the restoration of essential services to guarantee the delivery of humanitarian aid; announced the merger of the Luanda and Nairobi peace processes into a single, strengthened framework; ordered that a meeting of the chiefs of defence forces of the EAC and SADC be held within five days to establish technical guidelines for securing Goma and the surrounding areas, and the immediate reopening of Goma airport; insisted on the need to resume direct negotiations with all parties, including the rebel group M23; called for the implementation of a plan to neutralise the FDLR and for modalities for the withdrawal of uninvited foreign armed forces from Congolese territory; agreed to establish regular consultations at least once a year.

a4942.speaker: EAC-SADC summit final communique (received by APA)
a4942.name: EAC-SADC summit final communique (received by APA)
a4942.speech: the participants expressed their condolences to the victims of the conflict and condemned the recent attacks on diplomatic missions in Kinshasa, stressing the urgency of a peaceful and lasting solution; the summit concluded with thanks to Tanzania for organising the meeting and a call for rapid and concerted action to restore stability in the east of the DRC.

a5153.speaker: Mthuli Ncube, Zimbabwe Finance Minister
a5153.name: Mthuli Ncube
a5153.title: Zimbabwe Finance Minister
a5153.speech: says Zimbabwe has been buying more sovereign insurance policies against natural disasters with the African Risk Capacity (ARC) Group since it took out a total payment of US$1.4 million against the 2019/20 drought.

a5257.speaker: Nathaniel Maphathe, Lesotho Electricity Company (LEC) Managing Director
a5257.name: Nathaniel Maphathe
a5257.title: Lesotho Electricity Company (LEC) Managing Director
a5257.speech: Revealed before the Public Accounts Committee (PAC) that LEC owes the Lesotho Electricity Generation Company (LEGCO) over M70 million, stating the debt relates to electricity supplied by LEGCO through the Ramarothole Solar Project ; confirmed that LEGCO was selling electricity to LEC, reiterating that LEC currently owes LEGCO over M70 million: "It is over M70 million."

a5257.speaker: Auditor-General's reports (Lesotho)
a5257.name: Auditor-General's reports (Lesotho)
a5257.speech: Raised concerns to which the PAC had summoned LEC and other officials to respond.

a5257.speaker: Nqosa Mahao, Professor, Basotho Action Party (BAP) leader
a5257.name: Nqosa Mahao
a5257.title: Professor, Basotho Action Party (BAP) leader
a5257.speech: Asked Ministry of Energy Principal Secretary Tankiso Phapano whether LEGCO had generated any income since its formation ; further inquired whether an Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) had been conducted before the commencement of Ramarothole Phase I.

a5257.speaker: Tankiso Phapano, Ministry of Energy Principal Secretary (PS)
a5257.name: Tankiso Phapano
a5257.title: Ministry of Energy Principal Secretary (PS)
a5257.speech: Said LEGCO had not collected any revenue directly from the Ramarothole project, and that instead it had been supported by the government to meet requirements for the project's second phase: "LEGCO was established specifically to manage electricity generation from Ramarothole" ; "The ultimate goal is for LEGCO to manage all generation projects in the country, not just Ramarothole. But since its formation, the only revenue it received was last year, through a government levy to ensure it qualifies for the next phase."

a5257.speaker: Machabana Lemphane-Letsie, PAC chairperson
a5257.name: Machabana Lemphane-Letsie
a5257.title: PAC chairperson
a5257.speech: Questioned whether LEGCO was selling electricity to LEC: "My understanding is that from the day Ramarothole began supplying electricity to LEC, payments were supposed to be made" ; "I do not know what kind of animal LEC is. It owes EDM, which has already cut off supply. It owes Eskom, which is about to follow suit. It owes 'Muela. And now it owes Ramarothole as well."

a5257.speaker: Letooane, Ministry of Finance and Development official
a5257.name: Letooane
a5257.title: Ministry of Finance and Development official
a5257.speech: Admitted that no Environmental Impact Assessment had been carried out prior to construction.

a5257.speaker: Tseliso Moroke, Revolution for Prosperity (RFP) legislator for Matala
a5257.name: Tseliso Moroke
a5257.title: Revolution for Prosperity (RFP) legislator for Matala
a5257.speech: Expressed concern that the lack of an EIA had already led to serious environmental degradation, including the formation of deep erosion gullies (dongas) which the government had to repair at significant cost: "The Phase I of Ramarothole resulted in dongas that cost the government M27 million to fix" ; "You proceeded with Phase I without conducting an Environmental Impact Assessment. That is a fundamental environmental oversight. You are unable to proceed with Phase II because of the foundational errors made in Phase I. The absence of environmental studies and the lack of an EIA clearly resulted in these problems. This confirms that the Ministry failed to perform due diligence before implementing the project."

a5511.speaker: Abul Manyuon Mayen, practising pharmacist specializing in medication usage and administration in Australia
a5511.name: Abul Manyuon Mayen
a5511.title: practising pharmacist specializing in medication usage and administration in Australia
a5511.speech: Proposed the development of software to regulate how patients access medications, highlighting the risks posed by South Sudanese individuals visiting multiple drug stores, and stressed that a detailed dispensing history would help identify patients misusing drugs, particularly codeine ; suggested implementing a monitoring tool to control the quantity of medication dispensed to patients: “One of the ways pharmacists can monitor drug abuse is through a software system that tracks medication given to each patient, including dates,” she explained during an interview with Eye Radio ; pointed out the current lack of dispensing history in South Sudan, where patients can easily move from one pharmacy to another without any record: “Right now, we're often not providing adequate information, even for those who are prescribed medication” ; stressed the urgent need for pharmacists and regulatory bodies to establish a software system that tracks medication history: “This software would be beneficial for doctors to determine if someone is misusing medication and allow them to adjust prescriptions accordingly.”

a5596.speaker: Federal Government of Somalia
a5596.name: Federal Government of Somalia
a5596.speech: Has strongly rejected recent media allegations suggesting the existence of a so-called "secret deal" between Somalia and the Kingdom of Sweden linking development aid to deportations.

a5596.speaker: Office of the Prime Minister of Somalia (official statement)
a5596.name: Office of the Prime Minister of Somalia (official statement)
a5596.speech: Described the claims as false, misleading, and unfounded, emphasizing that Somalia has no secret or conditional arrangement with any partner regarding the return of its nationals or the allocation of development assistance ; "The cooperation between Somalia and Sweden is long-standing, transparent, and grounded in mutual respect and international law" ; underscored that all engagements between the two nations are conducted through formal diplomatic channels and are subject to cabinet oversight and institutional accountability ; clarified that all development assistance to Somalia is managed through transparent mechanisms, including the World Bank, United Nations agencies, and the Federal Government's central financial system (Country System) ; reaffirmed Somalia's commitment to upholding transparency and accountability in all its international partnerships and development cooperation frameworks.

a5631.speaker: Mohamed Malick Fall, United Nations Resident and Humanitarian Coordinator in Nigeria
a5631.name: Mohamed Malick Fall
a5631.title: United Nations Resident and Humanitarian Coordinator in Nigeria
a5631.speech: Has called on the private sector to fill the gap in funding development in Nigeria, and said Nigeria and other African countries should begin to think of local sourcing of funds for development ; "We are entering a new era where ODA, where development financing, where humanitarian financing would never be the way it has been for the past decade." ; "This is why we think that it is time for us to focus on what kind of alternative model will give the most value for financing development in a context like the one of Nigeria." ; "And today financing development cannot find any more resource than the domestic resources."

a5631.speaker: Mohamed Malick Fall, United Nations Resident and Humanitarian Coordinator in Nigeria
a5631.name: Mohamed Malick Fall
a5631.title: United Nations Resident and Humanitarian Coordinator in Nigeria
a5631.speech: Said the scheduled Africa Social Impact Summit is timely as it aimed at addressing the gaps of development.

a5631.speaker: Abubakar Suleiman, Chief Executive Officer of Sterling Banks Plc
a5631.name: Abubakar Suleiman
a5631.title: Chief Executive Officer of Sterling Banks Plc
a5631.speech: Said the summit aimed at providing space "where anyone who is trying to have a big impact can come and meet other like-minded people who are trying to do the same thing."

a5733.speaker: Caleb Mutfwang, Governor of Plateau State (statement through his media aide Gyang Bere)
a5733.name: Caleb Mutfwang
a5733.title: Governor of Plateau State (statement through his media aide Gyang Bere)
a5733.speech: Extended his heartfelt condolences to the families of those who lost their lives and to the government and people of Borno State.

a5733.speaker: Ngo Josephine Piyo, Deputy Governor of Plateau State
a5733.name: Ngo Josephine Piyo
a5733.title: Deputy Governor of Plateau State
a5733.speech: Emphasized that Plateau State stands in solidarity with the people of Borno in their time of grief and hardship, noting that the support demonstrated a shared sense of humanity and compassion during this difficult period; conveying Governor Mutfwang’s message of sympathy: “The news of this tragic event reached Plateau State with deep concern. We are painfully aware of the widespread devastation caused by the floods, which have ravaged entire communities, displacing families and destroying homes, livelihoods, and critical infrastructure.” ; “The people of Borno are in dire need of humanitarian assistance, and our hearts go out to all who have been affected.”

a5733.speaker: Caleb Mutfwang, Governor of Plateau State
a5733.name: Caleb Mutfwang
a5733.title: Governor of Plateau State
a5733.speech: Praised the swift response of both Governor Babagana Umara Zulum and the federal government in addressing the crisis, and urged philanthropists, organizations, and well-meaning individuals to contribute to the relief efforts: “As a token of our solidarity, the Plateau State government is providing these relief materials to support ongoing efforts. While we know these items cannot replace what has been lost, we hope they bring some comfort during this difficult time. We stand united with Borno State, and we pray that such disasters never occur again.”

a5733.speaker: Babagana Umara Zulum, Governor of Borno State
a5733.name: Babagana Umara Zulum
a5733.title: Governor of Borno State
a5733.speech: Expressed deep gratitude to the government and people of Plateau State for their generous support, acknowledging that this act of kindness would further strengthen the bond between Plateau and Borno States: “Our administration remains committed to providing relief and improving the living conditions of our people. The solidarity shown by Governor Mutfwang and the people of Plateau reinforces the strong ties we share, and we are thankful for this intervention.”

a5823.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a5823.name: Donald Trump
a5823.title: US President
a5823.speech: Decided on the suspension of American international aid, with the objective of reassessing and realigning United States foreign aid ; "The United States foreign aid industry and bureaucracy are not aligned with American interests and in many cases are antithetical to American values. They serve to destabilize world peace by promoting in foreign countries ideas that are directly opposed to harmonious and stable relations within and among countries." Such is the conviction of Donald Trump that motivates the suspension of American aid.

a5823.speaker: Donald Trump, US President (executive order of 20 January)
a5823.name: Donald Trump
a5823.title: US President (executive order of 20 January)
a5823.speech: Indicated that it is the policy of the United States that no further foreign assistance shall be disbursed in a manner that is not fully aligned with the foreign policy of the President of the United States; decrees a 90-day pause in United States foreign development assistance to assess the efficiency of programmes and their consistency with American foreign policy; instructs all department and agency heads responsible for United States foreign development assistance programmes to immediately pause new obligations and disbursements of development assistance funds to foreign countries, implementing non-governmental organisations, international organisations and contractors pending review; indicates that the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) must enforce this pause through its apportionment authority ; "New obligations and disbursements of foreign development assistance funds may resume for a programme before the end of the 90-day period if a review is conducted and if the Secretary of State or his designee, in consultation with the director of the OMB, decides to continue the programme in the same or a modified form. In addition, any other new foreign assistance programme and obligation must be approved by the Secretary of State or his designee, in consultation with the director of the OMB," Donald Trump indicated in his order of 20 January.

a5884.speaker: Adrian Njau, Acting Executive Director of the East African Business Council (EABC)
a5884.name: Adrian Njau
a5884.title: Acting Executive Director of the East African Business Council (EABC)
a5884.speech: "We are thrilled to partner with AfDB on this vital project that paves the way for stronger regional value chains, greater market access, and inclusive growth that benefits businesses and communities across East Africa" ; "This initiative demonstrates the power of partnerships in transforming our region's industrial landscape."

a5884.speaker: EABC leaders
a5884.name: EABC leaders
a5884.speech: Emphasized the project's alignment with the council's mission to promote a conducive business environment and sustainable, private sector-driven growth.

a5884.speaker: EAC Industrialization Policy and Strategy (2012-2032)
a5884.name: EAC Industrialization Policy and Strategy (2012-2032)
a5884.speech: Has set an ambitious goal of raising the manufacturing sector's share of GDP to at least 25% from the current average of 10% by 2032.

a5899.speaker: The Taliban
a5899.name: The Taliban
a5899.speech: Said that a team of Indian officials has met the acting foreign minister of Afghanistan to discuss bilateral ties and humanitarian aid, in what was the first such visit to Kabul since the group took control of the country in 2021.

a5899.speaker: Abdul Qahar Balkhi, Taliban foreign ministry spokesperson
a5899.name: Abdul Qahar Balkhi
a5899.title: Taliban foreign ministry spokesperson
a5899.speech: Said on Twitter that the minister called the visit a “good beginning in ties between the two countries”.

a5899.speaker: Mawlawi Amir Khan Muttaqi, Taliban administration’s acting foreign minister (reported by Balkhi)
a5899.name: Mawlawi Amir Khan Muttaqi
a5899.title: Taliban administration’s acting foreign minister (reported by Balkhi)
a5899.speech: Called the visit a “good beginning in ties between the two countries” ; expressed gratitude for the Indian humanitarian and medical assistance to Afghanistan, stressing the importance of the resumption of projects by India, its diplomatic presence in Afghanistan and the provision of consular services to Afghans, particularly to Afghan students and patients.

a5899.speaker: Arindam Bagchi, Indian foreign ministry spokesperson
a5899.name: Arindam Bagchi
a5899.title: Indian foreign ministry spokesperson
a5899.speech: Asked if New Delhi now officially recognised the Taliban administration, told reporters they were “reading far too much into the visit” ; declined to say when the embassy might be reopened, except to say that local staff had continued to function and ensure proper maintenance and upkeep of its premises there.

a5899.speaker: Indian foreign ministry (statement)
a5899.name: Indian foreign ministry (statement)
a5899.speech: Said earlier in a statement that the officials would oversee the delivery of humanitarian assistance and visit areas targeted by Indian-backed programmes or projects; said India has donated about 20,000 tons of wheat, 13 tons of medicines, 500,000 doses of Covid-19 vaccine, and items of winter clothing, with more medicine and food grains on the way.

a6080.speaker: Elon Musk, head of the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE)
a6080.name: Elon Musk
a6080.title: head of the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE)
a6080.speech: Accused USAID of funding projects he deemed “absurd”, such as transgender operas or pro-DEI musicals ; with his penchant for incendiary tweets and sensational revelations on X (formerly Twitter), his posts highlighted the spending judged most extravagant, arousing as much admiration as concern.

a6154.speaker: National Planning Commission (NPC)
a6154.name: National Planning Commission (NPC)
a6154.speech: Has announced that the first National Five-Year Medium-Term Development Plan (MTDP) under Tanzania's Vision 2050 (Dira 2050) is expected to be completed by November this year.

a6154.speaker: Dr Fred Msemwa, NPC Executive Secretary
a6154.name: Dr Fred Msemwa
a6154.title: NPC Executive Secretary
a6154.speech: "The initial Medium-Term Development Plan for 2026-2030 is expected to be ready by November. This is a crucial step because it lays the foundation for the implementation of Dira 2050." He explained that the 25-year Long-Term Perspective Plan will guide the implementation of Dira 2050, providing an overarching framework for annual and five-year development plans. Dr Msemwa described the upcoming MTDP as a launchpad for the long-term vision, translating broad national goals into actionable and measurable priorities. The LTPP review, he noted, was conducted in five working groups, which examined the plan in detail and reviewed relevant policies and legal frameworks to ensure smoother implementation ; Dr Msemwa said the NPC is now tasked with developing the Framework for the Fourth Five-Year Development Plan (FYDP IV), expected to be ready for stakeholder review and consultation by November.

a6154.speaker: Ambassador Moses Kusiluka, Chief Secretary
a6154.name: Ambassador Moses Kusiluka
a6154.title: Chief Secretary
a6154.speech: In his closing remarks, directed all permanent secretaries and their deputies to disseminate information about Dira 2050 within their ministries, ensuring every civil servant understands the document's content and goals. "I am taking onboard everything that Dr Msemwa has presented as part of the national agenda. This should not be seen as coming solely from the NPC, but as a collective requirement for all of us." He added that all public policies must be reviewed and aligned with Dira 2050 before it becomes operational in July 2026. On aligning public service delivery with the Vision, the Chief Secretary reaffirmed the government's commitment to modernising public services to meet the standards and expectations set out in the Vision.

a6154.speaker: Professor Kitila Mkumbo, Minister of State in the President's Office (Planning and Investment)
a6154.name: Professor Kitila Mkumbo
a6154.title: Minister of State in the President's Office (Planning and Investment)
a6154.speech: At the launch, stressed the importance of a strong, results-oriented implementation framework to drive the Vision forward. "This framework must eliminate inefficiencies and demand responsible leadership, rigorous execution and accountability." He stressed the need for a mindset shift, one that prioritises action over rhetoric and tangible outcomes over promises ; "Tanzania will not tolerate weak execution of its development plans," he stated, highlighting the need for policy alignment, institutional capacity and sectoral collaboration ; Prof Mkumbo acknowledged that difficult decisions will be necessary to establish Tanzania as a self-reliant, investment-driven economy.

a6260.speaker: Fiscal Responsibility Commission (FRC), Adamawa State
a6260.name: Fiscal Responsibility Commission (FRC)
a6260.title: Adamawa State
a6260.speech: Has pledged to work assiduously in partnership with other relevant agencies to block all leakages in the Internally Generated Revenue (IGR) of the State.

a6260.speaker: Umar Daware, Executive Chairman of the Fiscal Responsibility Commission (FRC)
a6260.name: Umar Daware
a6260.title: Executive Chairman of the Fiscal Responsibility Commission (FRC)
a6260.speech: Explained that the two-day event had afforded participants the opportunity to discover many factors that are responsible for poor budget performance, adding that action would be taken to address the leakages: “We have discovered so many factors responsible for poor budget implementation and we have spoken to ourselves both institutionally and individually to address them.” ; “We need to improve our budget performance in terms of revenues and expenditures, by so doing, it will not only enhance the development of the State, but also improve the ranking of Adamawa State in terms of fiscal accountability and transparency.” ; “There are leakages. Leakages are in form of non-remittance of what is due to the State Government, due to some of the inefficiencies of mechanisms on ground.” ; “We believe that when we address them and close up the gaps, it will improve revenue perfomance of Adamawa State.”

a6260.speaker: Umar Daware, Executive Chairman of the Fiscal Responsibility Commission (FRC)
a6260.name: Umar Daware
a6260.title: Executive Chairman of the Fiscal Responsibility Commission (FRC)
a6260.speech: Pointed out that the inefficiencies in revenue collection border on both individuals and institutions involved, and underscored the need for capacity building for revenue collectors as well as effective monitoring of the revenue collection for optimal performance.

a6260.speaker: Ayuba Tanko Audu, Adamawa State Commissioner for Water Resources
a6260.name: Ayuba Tanko Audu
a6260.title: Adamawa State Commissioner for Water Resources
a6260.speech: Commended the organisers of the two-day interactive session between members of the Adamawa State House of Assembly and some relevant Heads of Agencies in the priority areas of health, education, and WASH, and observed with joy that the event has deepened and cemented the synergy between the legislative and executive arms of government.

a6260.speaker: Ayuba Tanko Audu, Adamawa State Commissioner for Water Resources
a6260.name: Ayuba Tanko Audu
a6260.title: Adamawa State Commissioner for Water Resources
a6260.speech: Assured that with the support of the legislative arm, the budgetary allocation to the Water, Sanitation and Hygiene sector would be scaled up, noting that in the last one month there has been an improvement on budget allocation to the WASH sector, and assuring that the budget performance in the WASH sector would increase to 70 per cent in 2024.

a6576.speaker: Atupele Muluzi, United Democratic Front (UDF) president
a6576.name: Atupele Muluzi
a6576.title: United Democratic Front (UDF) president
a6576.speech: Says his party is open to go into an alliance with any like-minded party ahead of the September 16 General Election to resolve problems stifling development in the country ; said "We will go into an alliance with any party so long as they align with our principles and policies of business first, getting rid of corruption and growing the economy" ; said UDF will enter into an alliance with the aim of saving Malawi from problems such as shortage of foreign exchange, high cost of living and food insecurity, and that the UDF wants to devise the right programmes and policies to attract investment and allow businesses to grow to stimulate the economy.

a6576.speaker: Atupele Muluzi, United Democratic Front (UDF) president
a6576.name: Atupele Muluzi
a6576.title: United Democratic Front (UDF) president
a6576.speech: On his meeting with Dalitso Kabambe and Enoch Chihana, said their discussion dwelt more on ensuring peace and that the elections are free and fair: "We have seen that there have been ugly scenes so we came together as leaders to talk because politics is not about violence, it is about issues."

a6576.speaker: Atupele Muluzi, United Democratic Front (UDF) president
a6576.name: Atupele Muluzi
a6576.title: United Democratic Front (UDF) president
a6576.speech: Warned that the era of relying on foreign aid is gone and that countries such as Malawi need visionary leaders who are ready to focus on trade and investment.

a6576.speaker: Dorothy Masinga, UDF regional governor for the South
a6576.name: Dorothy Masinga
a6576.title: UDF regional governor for the South
a6576.speech: Said UDF supporters want a clean government and any alliance should involve politicians who have no record of corruption.

a6576.speaker: UTM Party
a6576.name: UTM Party
a6576.speech: Said it has started holding electoral coalition talks with UDF, Aford, People's Party (PP) and other opposition parties in preparation for the September 16 General Election.

a6576.speaker: Felix Njawala, UTM Party spokesperson
a6576.name: Felix Njawala
a6576.title: UTM Party spokesperson
a6576.speech: Said the party believed that an alliance can work out despite UTM Party having had a bad experience in the governing Tonse Alliance, and that the goal of the alliance is to strengthen the parties' presence in the next elections and save Malawians from the current challenges ; said "There is a lot of anticipation, and anxiety on the political landscape because people are really looking forward to an entity that can transform this country and change their lives" ; declined to give more details, saying the talks are ongoing and that the major focus is not on who will be on the ballot ; said UTM was yet to discuss the issue with the Democratic Progressive Party (DPP).

a6576.speaker: Dyson Jangia, UDF spokesperson
a6576.name: Dyson Jangia
a6576.title: UDF spokesperson
