a6576.speech: Said the party has been having electoral alliance discussions with several parties, adding it is not strange that leaders of UTM Party, UDF and Aford met ; said "We are looking for a trustworthy partner, somebody we can rely on. Not a partner who would eventually break what you agreed on. So, we will be looking at the track record, trustworthiness of whoever is there to partner with."

a6576.speaker: Annie Amatullah Maluwa, Aford spokesperson
a6576.name: Annie Amatullah Maluwa
a6576.title: Aford spokesperson
a6576.speech: Also confirmed the talks, but said Aford is talking to other parties in opposition and that Malawians will be informed of the outcome of the talks.

a6576.speaker: George Chaima, political analyst
a6576.name: George Chaima
a6576.title: political analyst
a6576.speech: Has said a combination of UTM Party, UDF, Aford and PP can make wonders if the parties strategise and make proper and binding agreements ; said the leaders of the parties have different strengths that if put together will have a great impact.

a6576.speaker: Peter Mukhito, Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) secretary general
a6576.name: Peter Mukhito
a6576.title: Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) secretary general
a6576.speech: Said last week that his party was in talks with several parties, including UTM Party, UDF, PP and Aford.

a6667.speaker: Katawa, group village head
a6667.name: Katawa
a6667.title: group village head
a6667.speech: Said in an interview yesterday that people around Kakoloha have been blaming the cracks in their houses on the blasts and are demanding compensation.

a6667.speaker: Report by Robert Chidothe, Rumphi Community Development officer
a6667.name: Report by Robert Chidothe
a6667.title: Rumphi Community Development officer
a6667.speech: Shows that communities wanted the company to construct a proper drainage system, rehabilitate access roads and provide building materials for a local primary school: "For instance, the potable water system installed was placed near a sewer area. The marketplace was described as too small and poorly built. The community expressed deep disappointment and a sense of betrayal."

a6667.speaker: He Chuanfeng, project manager for China Henan International Cooperation Group (Chicco)
a6667.name: He Chuanfeng
a6667.title: project manager for China Henan International Cooperation Group (Chicco)
a6667.speech: Said people were failing to understand that development assistance is not obligatory: "As a contractor, it is not obligatory to provide assistance to the local community, if this is done it is done for social upliftment and a gesture from the company."

a6667.speaker: Engineer Ammiel Champiti, Roads Authority chief executive officer
a6667.name: Engineer Ammiel Champiti
a6667.title: Roads Authority chief executive officer
a6667.speech: Said the issues for Lot 4 were identical to Lots 1, 2 and 3, but added that people around Lot 4 are motivated by "baseless demands" as efforts being made by people are criminal in nature.

a6670.speaker: Niger (government)
a6670.name: Niger (government)
a6670.speech: Declared that it had demanded the departure of the European Union ambassador, Mr. Salvador Pinto Da Franca, and his replacement as soon as possible, and specified that this decision was taken at its own initiative and not that of the EU.

a6670.speaker: Nigerien Ministry of Foreign Affairs (official statement)
a6670.name: Nigerien Ministry of Foreign Affairs (official statement)
a6670.speech: Denounced "unsolicited" EU aid, distributed through NGOs "in total opacity."

a6670.speaker: Nigerien government
a6670.name: Nigerien government
a6670.speech: Asserted that it had never issued an appeal for international aid, having decided to manage the situation with its own funds ; asserted that the unauthorized operations continued despite the ambassador being summoned on 14 October 2024 and given an explicit warning.

a6670.speaker: Nigerien authorities
a6670.name: Nigerien authorities
a6670.speech: Accused the ambassador of having proceeded "unilaterally" in allocating the grant to several NGOs, notably the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC), the Danish Refugee Council (DRC) and Cooperazione Internazionale (COOPI), and particularly criticized the "arbitrary" distribution of the funds by region.

a6670.speaker: Niamey (Nigerien government)
a6670.name: Niamey (Nigerien government)
a6670.speech: Announced the launch of an audit into the management of the funds and formally asks the European Union to do the same in order to "know the real use and destination of the sums allocated to the NGOs concerned."

a6670.speaker: European Union
a6670.name: European Union
a6670.speech: Expressed "its profound disagreement with the allegations," maintaining that humanitarian aid is provided "in a neutral, impartial and independent manner" through United Nations agencies and international organizations ; Brussels denounced any "instrumentalization of humanitarian aid for political ends" while reaffirming its willingness to support the Nigerien population.

a6947.speaker: African Development Bank (AfDB)
a6947.name: African Development Bank (AfDB)
a6947.speech: Said South Africa must accelerate structural reforms to offset global challenges that include US President Donald Trump's trade war, as it cut the nation's economic forecast, lowering its forecast for Africa's most-industrialised economy to a meager 0.8% this year from a previous estimate of 1.6% in an update to its Country Focus Report for South Africa, and named other risks to the outlook including funding cuts for development assistance and an economic slowdown in China.

a6947.speaker: African Development Bank (AfDB)
a6947.name: African Development Bank (AfDB)
a6947.speech: "Industries such as agriculture, which rely heavily on US market access, will be particularly vulnerable." ; "In the short-term, this could slow economic activity, decrease firm profitability, and constrain job creation in export-linked industries." ; said domestic risks to the economic outlook include "infrastructure gaps electricity shortages, logistical bottlenecks, and fiscal vulnerabilities arising from the bailout of state-owned enterprises."

a6947.speaker: Akhona Peter, AfDB country economist
a6947.name: Akhona Peter
a6947.title: AfDB country economist
a6947.speech: "This is mainly on the fact that we expect trade tensions to pretty much affect net exports negatively," said on Wednesday at an event near Pretoria.

a6947.speaker: South Africa's Treasury
a6947.name: South Africa's Treasury
a6947.speech: In May trimmed its growth forecast for the year to 1.4% from a prior 1.9%, citing geopolitical tensions including Trump's trade levies.

a6947.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a6947.name: Donald Trump
a6947.title: US President
a6947.speech: Said on Wednesday that he is not considering delaying the tariffs again.

a7169.speaker: Ms Joyce Befu, Bottom Up leader of delegation
a7169.name: Ms Joyce Befu
a7169.title: Bottom Up leader of delegation
a7169.speech: Has reminded us to remind the politicians that the manifestos that they presented (over 20 for president, over 1,000 for MPs and countless others for ward councillors) to the Malawi Electoral Commission (MEC) are too bulky and too numerous for us to read them all.

a7169.speaker: National Planning Commission (NPC)
a7169.name: National Planning Commission (NPC)
a7169.speech: Has identified enablers which include mindset change, effective governance institutions and systems, enhanced public sector performance, human capital development, environmental sustainability, economic infrastructure, and private sector dynamism.

a7193.speaker: Recent figures from humanitarian organisations
a7193.name: Recent figures from humanitarian organisations
a7193.speech: According to recent figures from humanitarian organisations, Nigeria is home to over 3.5 million internally displaced persons.

a7193.speaker: Sarah Yakubu, 36-year-old displaced woman from Logo, Benue State, living in the Daudu IDP camp
a7193.name: Sarah Yakubu
a7193.title: 36-year-old displaced woman from Logo, Benue State, living in the Daudu IDP camp
a7193.speech: “We queue for food that never comes,” she says. “Sometimes NGOs bring rice and oil, but what about clean water? What about education for our children? What about our future?”

a7193.speaker: Camp volunteer in Borno (anonymous, asked not to be named)
a7193.name: Camp volunteer in Borno (anonymous
a7193.title: asked not to be named)
a7193.speech: “I know of girls as young as 13 being pregnant here,” says a camp volunteer in Borno. “Many men, including some of those working with camp authorities, take advantage of them. No one talks about it. The government does not care.”

a7193.speaker: Abdul, 44-year-old farmer from Guma LGA
a7193.name: Abdul
a7193.title: 44-year-old farmer from Guma LGA
a7193.speech: “Going home means choosing between death and starvation,” says Abdul. “Even if we return, who will protect us? The same government that didn't protect us the first time?”

a7229.speaker: Uche T. Onyebadi, USA-based Nigerian scholar, Associate Professor at Texas Christian University
a7229.name: Uche T. Onyebadi
a7229.title: USA-based Nigerian scholar, Associate Professor at Texas Christian University
a7229.speech: "These are the words of USA-based Nigerian scholar, Associate Professor Uche T. Onyebadi of Texas Christian University" - cited as the author of the words that open the article, which the writer says resonate with the situation of the Botswana National Front (BNF).

a7305.speaker: Florence Makumene, 53-year-old HIV-positive woman from Zimbabwe
a7305.name: Florence Makumene
a7305.title: 53-year-old HIV-positive woman from Zimbabwe
a7305.speech: "I was deteriorating, but after starting treatment, I made a remarkable recovery."

a7305.speaker: Florence Makumene, 53-year-old HIV-positive woman from Zimbabwe
a7305.name: Florence Makumene
a7305.title: 53-year-old HIV-positive woman from Zimbabwe
a7305.speech: "We feel abandoned; there's no one to help us" ; "We are reverting to the dark times when being HIV positive was synonymous with death. We urgently need assistance."

a7305.speaker: Health officials and experts across the continent
a7305.name: Health officials and experts across the continent
a7305.speech: Are urgently calling for the resumption of PEPFAR, fearing that the dismantling of these essential services could set back progress by decades.

a7305.speaker: Winnie Byanyima, Executive Director of the United Nations AIDS program (UNAIDS)
a7305.name: Winnie Byanyima
a7305.title: Executive Director of the United Nations AIDS program (UNAIDS)
a7305.speech: "If the American government doesn't reconsider and uphold its leadership... lives will be lost" ; Informed The Associated Press that the funding halt could lead to a rise in AIDS cases, causing "panic, fear, and confusion" across numerous African nations: "We could see an increase of 3.4 million AIDS orphans."

a7305.speaker: United Nations AIDS program (UNAIDS)
a7305.name: United Nations AIDS program (UNAIDS)
a7305.speech: According to the programme, AIDS-related deaths have plummeted by 69% since their peak in 2004, and new HIV infections have dropped by 60% since 1995.

a7305.speaker: Many experts
a7305.name: Many experts
a7305.speech: Attribute this turnaround to PEPFAR, initiated by Republican President George W. Bush, which has primarily focused on Africa, saving countless lives through a program that provides crucial medication to manage HIV.

a7305.speaker: Kenyan officials
a7305.name: Kenyan officials
a7305.speech: According to officials, in Kenya over 40,000 workers are at risk of being laid off due to the aid freeze.

a7305.speaker: Lesotho's Health Ministry
a7305.name: Lesotho's Health Ministry
a7305.speech: Has reached out to final-year medical students and recent graduates, encouraging them to volunteer at local health centres to fill staffing gaps.

a7305.speaker: Marco Rubio, U.S. Secretary of State
a7305.name: Marco Rubio
a7305.title: U.S. Secretary of State
a7305.speech: On January 28 announced waivers aimed at ensuring the continuation of lifesaving treatments and other essential components of PEPFAR; Rubio has expressed his support for PEPFAR, although he has raised some concerns.

a7305.speaker: Federal judge (US)
a7305.name: Federal judge (US)
a7305.speech: Recently mandated that the Trump administration temporarily lift the freeze on foreign funding, dismissing the claim that the administration was providing waivers to facilitate some funding; the judge pointed out that no waiver system was in place at that time.

a7305.speaker: Health experts and activists
a7305.name: Health experts and activists
a7305.speech: Have voiced their discontent with the waivers issued by the Trump administration, which limit access to treatment for certain populations.

a7402.speaker: Experts of the FAO and of the directorate of veterinary services of the Ministry of Animal and Fishery Resources of Côte d'Ivoire
a7402.name: Experts of the FAO and of the directorate of veterinary services of the Ministry of Animal and Fishery Resources of Côte d'Ivoire
a7402.speech: In presentations, made known and explained the problem of antimicrobial resistance; explained that one speaks of Antimicrobial Resistance when micro-organisms, such as bacteria, viruses, parasites or fungi, become resistant to antimicrobial treatments to which they were previously susceptible; stressed that the more microbes are exposed to pharmaceutical products, such as antibiotics, the more likely they are to adapt, and that this resistance occurs when microbes develop mechanisms that make them resistant to the drugs meant to eliminate them.

a7402.speaker: Amy Carine Dongo, national coordinator of ECTAD (FAO)
a7402.name: Amy Carine Dongo
a7402.title: national coordinator of ECTAD (FAO)
a7402.speech: Stressed that this year's theme calls on the global community to intensify awareness-raising and to take concrete measures to prevent and combat antimicrobial resistance: “Solutions are within reach, but they require concerted action. Every measure taken today helps to guarantee the health of tomorrow,” calling on communities for a responsible use of antimicrobials and for the strengthening of surveillance systems.

a7402.speaker: Fadiga Haïda Kaly, technical adviser, speaking on behalf of the Minister of Animal and Fishery Resources of Côte d'Ivoire
a7402.name: Fadiga Haïda Kaly
a7402.title: technical adviser, speaking on behalf of the Minister of Animal and Fishery Resources of Côte d'Ivoire
a7402.speech: Stressed that this silent but alarming scourge threatens public health, the agricultural and animal production system, as well as global food security; indicated that about 1.27 million direct deaths are attributable each year to antimicrobial resistance, adding that this phenomenon compromises the treatment of serious diseases, in both humans and animals: “If no significant action is undertaken, projections estimate that this number could reach 10 million deaths per year by 2050, thus exceeding mortality due to cancer,” she warned.
